title: Alex McKenzie Collection of Computer Networking Development Records
long_description: The collection contains general notes, protocol notes, experiments notes, legal/political notes, security notes and a newsletter file regarding the International Packet Network Working Group (INWG.) [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/242]

title: Association for Computing Machinery
long_description: Selected images and materials of this educational and scientific computing society founded in 1947 as the Eastern Association for Computing Machinery, documenting its administration, operations, projects and its Special Interest Groups (SIGs) which represent virtually every major area of computing. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/318]

title: Burroughs Corporation Records
long_description: The collection contains the records of the Burroughs Corporation, and its predecessors the American Arithmometer Company and Burroughs Adding Machine Company. Materials include corporate records, photographs, films and video tapes, scrap books, papers of employees and records of companies acquired by Burroughs during the companies tenure in the adding machine and computer industry, such as the System Development Corporation, Charles R. Hadley Company, Control Instrument Company, ElectroData and Todd Company. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/222]

title: CBI Fragile Publications
long_description: A set of fragile materials from the collections of the Charles Babbage Institute.

title: CBI Oral History Collections
long_description: The Charles Babbage Institute holds one of the world's largest collections of research-grade oral history interviews relating to the history of computers, software, and networking. Most of the oral histories have been developed in conjunction with grant-funded research projects on topics such as the development of the software industry, the influence of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA), and the early history of computer science departments. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/24]

title: CBI Reference Files
long_description: The Charles Babbage Institute Reference Files contain oral history transcripts, reference photographs and audiovisual material, and reference files on a number of different topics relating to the history of computing. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/24]

title: Conference on Data Systems Languages Records
long_description: The Conference on Data Systems Languages Records collection contains minutes, correspondence, reports, documentation for Nice Standard Control Language (NICOLA), the Journal of Development, and other publications from several CODASYL committees and task groups. Most of the collection consists of photocopies. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/35]

title: Control Data Corporation Records
long_description: The Control Data Corporation Records documents the company's operations, goals, plans, and products from its inception in 1957 to 1992, and includes information about CDC's corporate philosophy and long-time president and CEO (1957-1986), William C. Norris. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/104]

title: Dean Eaker Papers and Publications
long_description: Dean has worked in the computer graphics space for more than 30 years, documenting it through production of publications and from an entrepreneurial standpoint. He is currently the owner of WiredAssets. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/7374]

title: Edmund C. Berkeley Papers
long_description: Contains correspondence, notes, memoranda, lists, reports, reference material, financial records, publications, posters, advertisements, photographs, and a videotape relating to Edmund Berkeley and Berkeley Enterprises. The earliest records in the collection relate to his insurance work, the applications of symbolic logic and computing machines to business, the formation of the Association for Computing Machinery, and his military service at Dahlgren. Later records focus on the publications and operations of Berkeley Enterprises as well as Berkeley's social activism. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/47]

title: International Y2K Cooperation Center Records
long_description: Collection contains the materials of the International Y2K Cooperation Center (IY2KCC), assembled during the year leading up to the year 2000 date conversion (a.k.a. Y2K). Includes country reports, news clippings, country questionnaires, country telephone directories, background materials on Y2K and IY2KCC, audio visual materials and papers of Bruce W. McConnell, director of IY2KCC. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/567]

title: The COOK Report on Internet Protocol
long_description: The COOK Report on Internet Protocol is a journal focused on Internet related technology and policy. It was started in the spring of 1992 by Gordon Cook, the journal’s sole editor and publisher, following an 18-month tenure at the United States Congress Office of Technology Assessment. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/418]

title: U.S. National Bureau of Standards Collection of Computer Literature
long_description: Collection contains reports, manuals and publications from corporations, government agencies, and academic computing centers covering a broad range of computer-related topics. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/3/resources/38]

title: Beadle's Weekly
long_description: Beadle's Weekly featured serialized stories from numerous authors presented in a story paper format. Marketed to both children and adults alike, this publication ran from 1882-1885.

title: Florence Slobodkin Papers
long_description: The Florence Slobodkin papers contain written material for titles by Florence Slobodkin, as well as personal materials and unpublished writing. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/4/resources/3299#]

title: Kerlan Collection Artwork
long_description: The Kerlan Collection at the University of Minnesota is one of the world's great children's literature archives. The Collection includes books, original manuscripts and illustrations, and related materials.

title: Log Cabin Library
long_description: The Log Cabin Library was a”dime novel" series published by Street and Smith featuring serialized stories from numerous authors.

title: Louis Slobodkin Papers
long_description: Louis Slobodkin's papers focus on his work as an author and illustrator of children's books. The collection contains production material for various titles published between 1943-1972, as well as correspondence with wife, Florence, artwork, and some miscellaneous material. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/4/resources/2806]

title: Old Cap. Collier Library
long_description: Old Cap. Collier was an American weekly focusing on detective stories involving various crimes and criminals. The collection housed in the University of Minnesota's Children's Literature Research Collection contains issues dating between 1883 and 1899.

title: Pulp Novel Covers
long_description: Images of pulp novel covers held in the collections of the University of Minnesota's Children's Literature Research Collections.

title: The Illustrated Police News
long_description: The Illustrated Police News was an American weekly focusing on stories of crime, criminals, and trials. The collection housed in the University of Minnesota's Children's Literature Research Collection contains issues dating between 1876 and 1896.

title: The Oz Collection
long_description: A personal collection of Oziana and other Baum-related children's literature collected by Laura Jane Musser throughout her lifetime. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/4/resources/2733]

title: The Pansy
long_description: The Pansy was issued in weekly parts as a Sunday school paper and then in numbers to mail subscribers. The collection housed in the University of Minnesota's Children's Literature Research Collection.

title: African American Literature
long_description: This collection contains images of book covers and jackets from books held by the Givens Collection. These images are a rich and diverse visual accompaniment to the books themselves and highlight the artistry of the book illustrators commissioned to visually represent the written word.

title: Countee Cullen Correspondence Collection
long_description: The collection consists of correspondence from Countee Cullen to his childhood friend William F. Brown, Jr., as well as miscellaneous items relating to Cullen's writing. Many letters are partially written in Latin, and concern Cullen's literary and scholarly pursuits. Cullen included in his letters many handwritten and manuscript copies of his poems, in addition to a few newspaper clippings of his published poems, and copies of the high school literary journal and newspaper for which Cullen wrote. Also included are several of Cullen's attempts at writing song lyrics, as well as a copy of a letter regarding this pursuit from a composer's bureau. The bulk of the correspondence is from the years 1918-1927. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/5/resources/330]

title: E. Ethelbert Miller Collection
long_description: Correspondence of E. Ethelbert Miller. A poet, essayist, editor and educator, Miller has published poetry collections and has edited several anthologies. [There are several Finding Aids available at: https://z.umn.edu/e-ethelbert-miller]

title: Givens Ephemera Collection
long_description: Includes press clippings, playbills, correspondence, and manuscripts excerpts/short drafts, and other ephemera about African-American history and culture. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/5/resources/7154]

title: Givens Pamphlet Collection
long_description: Pamphlets collected by the University of Minnesota's Givens Collection of African American Literature.

title: Givens Playbills and Programs Collection
long_description: African American theater playbills and programs collected by the University of Minnesota's Givens Collection of African American Literature.

title: Lou Bellamy Rare Book Collection
long_description: Lou Bellamy (1944- ) is the founder and co-artistic director of Penumbra Theatre. During his tenure, Penumbra has evolved into one of America’s premier theaters dedicated to dramatic exploration of African American life.

title: Narratives by Formerly Enslaved Peoples Collection
long_description: Collection includes transcripts of narratives by formerly enslaved peoples, recorded for the Works Progress Administration (WPA) Federal Writers’ Project in the 1930s. The transcripts were recorded by Carrie Campbell, with accounts taken from formerly enslaved individuals living in Coahoma County, Mississippi. The narratives were housed in a shirt box in a Mississippi closet until given to a University of Minnesota American Studies graduate student Stephen Wiley in the 1970s, who donated the materials to the Givens Collection in 1986.

title: Penumbra Theatre Company Records
long_description: Penumbra Theatre Company is the largest professional African American theater in the United States. Founded in 1976 by Lou Bellamy, the theater is located in St. Paul, Minnesota, in the Hallie Q. Brown Community Center. Since 2014, Lou Bellamy and Sarah Bellamy have served as Co-Artistic Directors. This collection contains the administrative records and artistic materials of Penumbra Theatre from the company's founding in 1976 through 2012. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/5/resources/331]

title: Penumbra Theatre Playbills
long_description: Penumbra Theatre Company is the largest professional African American theater in the United States. Founded in 1976 by Lou Bellamy, the theater is located in St. Paul, Minnesota, in the Hallie Q. Brown Community Center. Since 2014, Lou Bellamy and Sarah Bellamy have served as Co-Artistic Directors. This collection contains playbills documenting the work of the Penumbra Theatre.

title: Sara Roberson Papers
long_description: Sara Roberson is a former Minneapolis Public School (MPS) teacher. Roberson is a graduate of Macalaster College in St. Paul and United Theological Seminary in Minneapolis. This collection includes materials from the 30+ years that Roberson taught for MPS as well as her mentorship and social justice work outside of the school system. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/5/resources/335]

title: Adunata dei refrattari FBI files collection
long_description: Copies of FBI files regarding the Italian American anarchist newspaper L'Adunata dei Refrattari, published in New York. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/8072]

title: Aloysius Mazewski Papers
long_description: The Aloysius Mazewski Papers relate directly to the two positions held by A. A. Mazewski in the Polish American community over the years: presidency of the Polish National Alliance and of the Polish American Congress. The records cover, roughly, the period of Mazewski’s leadership of both organizations, that is the years from 1968 to his death in 1988. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4897]

title: American Hellenic Educational Progressive Association (AHEPA) Records
long_description: A fraternal, cultural, and social organization, the Order of AHEPA (American Hellenic Educational Progressive Association) was founded in 1922 to fight discrimination and to help newly arrived Greeks adapt to American life. Today the Order has over 50,000 members with greater than 500 chapters in the United States, Canada, Australia, Greece, and Cyprus. This collection contains correspondence pertaining to the local chapters of AHEPA for the period of 1922-1950. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/3911]

title: Arab American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Arab American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Armenian American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Armenian American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Belarusan American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Belarusan American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Bureau for Intercultural Education (New York, New York) Records
long_description: Records (ca. 1940-1960) of the Bureau for International Education (New York) include correspondence, minutes, interviews, articles, publications, and reports. Also included are tapes and transcriptions of tapes of Stewart Cole. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/5105]

title: Carpatho-Rusin American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Carpatho-Rusin American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Croatian American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Czech-Bohemian American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Czech-Bohemian American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Daughters of Penelope Oral History Project
long_description: Oral histories conducted with Greek Americans in 1979-1980 by the Daughters of Penelope Greek American organization in Minnesota. Some background and biographical information about the speakers is included in the collection in paper form. [Finding Aid available at http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/3989]

title: Digitizing Immigrant Letters
long_description: The Digitizing Immigrant Letters Project aims to make available on-line letters from the IHRC Archives and other collections (private individuals, partner institutions) that were written between 1850 and 1970 both by immigrants (the so-called “America letters”) and to immigrants (“homeland letters”). Global and multilingual in scope, the project encourages scholars, teachers, students and the public to interpret letters that express emotion and intimacy among loved ones separated by migration. [Project website available at: https://ihrca.umn.edu/immigrant-letters/]

title: Estonian American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Estonian American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Finnish American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Finnish American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Finnish Socialist Club, Astoria, Oregon Records
long_description: Minutes (1912-1915), in Finnish, of the Finnish Socialist Club (Astoria, Ore.), Board of Directors. Although the minutes deal mainly with business affairs, they indirectly reflect much of the cultural and political activity in the Astoria Finnish socialist community during this time. For example, the minutes for 1913 include records of donations to the striking copper miners in Michigan. Except for Board minutes published in the newspaper Toveri, these are the only known extant minutes of the Finnish Socialist Club of Astoria, Oregon. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4133]

title: Fort Velona Papers
long_description: Papers (1919-1962) of Italian American socialist Fort Velona (1893-1965) contain correspondence, photographs, newspaper clippings, articles, cartoons and published items. Velona's work appeared in La Parola del Popolo (Chicago), Nuovo Mundo, and La Stampa Libera. The bulk of the collection consists of originals of caricatures and cartoons dealing with domestic and international labor and politics. Issues of and clippings from La Parola del Popolo are also included. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4691#]

title: Foundational Collection of Immigration Oral Histories
long_description: Foundational Collection of Immigration Oral Histories offers rare and unique content on national racial and social justice histories, and on education and immigration. These interviews, on the formation of the intercultural education movement and the work of early social service agencies, thus discuss multiculturalism, race, and ethnicity in America. These interviews are with pioneering immigration historians and the leadership of the Common Council for American Unity (and its important publication Common Ground) and include topics such as African Americans, anti-Semitism, Communism, International Institutes, and prominent individuals such as Louis Adamic and Langston Hughes.

title: Greek American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Greek American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Hugo Skrastins Papers
long_description: Hugo Skrastins was born in Latvia in 1914 where he was active in theatrical and publishing activities. He left Latvia during WWII and came to the U.S. in 1950.Settling in Minneapolis, he resumed his publishing career producing the Latvian periodical Tilts and later the photo magazine Voyageur, a publication devoted to Great Lakes area ethnic culture and the environment. This collection contains correspondence files related to Skrastins's activities as publisher of Voyageur magazine and as proprietor of Hugo Skrastins Film Company. Correspondents are primarily advertisers, contributors, and production associates for Skrastins's magazine and films. Also included are several issues of Voyageur. [Finding Aid available at http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4572]

title: Hungarian American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Hungarian American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Immigrant Stories
long_description:
Immigrant Stories is a research and archiving project run by the Immigration History Research Center (IHRC) at the University of Minnesota. Immigrant Stories helps immigrants, refugees, and their family members create digital stories: brief videos with images, text, and audio about a personal experience.

This project defines "immigrant" broadly. Our collection contains digital stories from people living outside their country of birth as well as stories created by their children and grandchildren. Immigrant Stories also welcomes stories from international students, international adoptees, and people who do not feel that their stories fit a particular, or just one, category. All stories are important, and we invite you to make a video and share yours with us.

title: Immigration History Research Center Archives General Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting immigrant history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Immigration History Research Center Archives Serials Collection
long_description: The newspapers and serials holdings of the Immigration History Research Center Archives (IHRCA) largely consist of materials published by immigrants after arriving in North America, and largely date from the 20th century.

title: International Institute of Minnesota Records
long_description: Records (ca. 1920-2004) of the International Institute of Minnesota include minutes of the membership Council and Board of Directors (on microfilm), administrative records, educational program information, department records, materials documenting group services and activities, special programs, projects, and publications, community and national contacts, publicity, music, travel literature, case files, correspondence, photographs, and miscellany. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4884]

title: Italian American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Italian American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Italians in Duluth Oral History Project
long_description: Oral History project undertaken by the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archive to document the experiences of Italian Americans in the city of Duluth, Minnesota.

title: Jaroslav de Zielinski Papers
long_description: The Jaroslav de Zielinski Papers consist of correspondence, handbills, manuscripts, programs, a scrapbook, and photographs. Also included are research notes of Robert C. Bryant and Edward A. Symans pertaining to Zielinski's life. Correspondence is predominantly with Zielinski's friend and pupil Edith V. Rann. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4777]

title: Joint Baltic American National Committee Records
long_description: This collection consists of administrative records for the Joint Baltic American National Committee, an organization that represents Baltic-American communities in conjunction with issues related to Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/5880]

title: La Prensa de Minnesota
long_description: La Prensa is a state-wide bilingual weekly newspaper for business, arts, and community news.</br></br> La Prensa es un periódico semanal de negocios, artes y noticias comunitarias.

title: Latvian American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Latvian American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Lehtinen Family Papers
long_description: Papers (1912-1995) of the Lehtinen Family consist of biographical information, photographs, postcards, newspaper clippings, materials documenting Finnish American life in places where Kaarle Lehtinen resided, primarily Montreal, Wisconsin; Newport, New Hampshire, and Lake Worth, Florida.: Finding aid available at https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4238</br></br> Lehtisen suvun paperiaineisto (1912-1995) sisältää elämänkerrallista tietoa, valokuvia, postikortteja, sanomalehtileikkeitä, amerikansuomalaista elämää dokumentoivia materiaaleja paikoista, joissa Kaarle Lehtinen asui, keskittyen paikkoihin Montreal, Wisconsin; Newport, New Hampshire ja Lake Worth, Florida.: Arkistoluettelo saatavilla osoitteessa https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4238

title: Mario Pavone Papers
long_description: The Mario Pavone collection contains New Jersey convention minutes and correspondence, 1968, 1970; and minutes, financial reports and memos relating to the Orphans' Home Commission. Included are photographs and a videotape of the orphans home. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4397]

title: Minnesota Oromo Oral History Project Records
long_description: Three oral histories conducted by Hibaa Roba of Crystal, Minnesota in 2022. Interviewees are Johara Mohammed, Tasissa Moti, and Ibrahim Roba, all immigrants from the Oromia region of Ethiopia. [Finding available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/11154]

title: Polish American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Polish American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Rachel Davis DuBois Papers
long_description: Papers (ca. 1917-1973) of Rachel Davis Dubois comprise both personal papers and organizational records and include correspondence; minutes; reports; publications; curricular materials; speeches; draft autobiography; newspaper clippings; loose photographs; scrapbooks of photographs; and various published and unpublished writings produced and received by DuBois. Also included are research files and phonograph records from "Americans All, Immigrants All" radio series for which DuBois served as consultant. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/5078]

title: Ralf William and Elsbeth (ne Müller) Adams Papers
long_description: Biographical materials, correspondence, and architectural drawings from the papers of Ralf William and Elsbeth Adams.

title: Rev. Kenneth Dexter Miller Papers
long_description: Kenneth Dexter Miller, a Presbyterian minister, was a leader in interdenominational efforts to make churches responsive to urban needs, especially the needs of ethnic minorities. The papers (1910-1969), of the Rev. Kenneth Dexter Miller (1887-1968) consist of correspondence; drafts, reviews and advertisements of his articles and books; memorabilia; personal journals; photographs; scrapbooks; and a stamp collection. The journals date from his time in Bohemia, and discuss religious attitudes of the Bohemians; and from his Siberian trek during World War I. Also included is correspondence of Miller's wife, Ethel P. Miller, with her college roommate, Mrs. O. K. Sherwin. Mrs. Miller's vita is also included. [Finding Aid available at http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4324]

title: Romanian American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Romanian American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Sheeko - Somali Youth Oral History Collection
long_description: Sheeko is a collection of Somali youth stories created by and for Somali youth. During 2010- 2011, a team of University of Minnesota Somali students conducted dozens of interviews with Somalis living outside of Somalia who were between the ages of 18-25. Many of the narrators lived in Minnesota, Minnesota and London, England. The project was centered at and sponsored by the Immigration History Research Center at the University of Minnesota. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/5039#]

title: Slovak American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Slovak American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Slovenian American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Slovenian American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Sucheng Chan Papers
long_description: Photocopies of journal articles and book chapters related to Asian American studies and Prof. Chan's interests. Some annotation. Books and periodicals were separated from the collection and catalogued individually. Material related to Chinese immigration and Chinese Americans can be found throughout the collection. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4938]

title: Ukrainian American Collection
long_description: Photographs and other archival materials documenting Ukrainian American history and culture from the University of Minnesota's Immigration History Research Center Archives.

title: Ukrainian Famine Survivors in Minnesota Oral History Project
long_description: Interviews with survivors (or their descendants) of the Ukrainian Famine (Holodomor) of the 1930s. The participants in the project live in Minnesota. Included are also transcripts of all interviews and translations for those in Ukrainian.

title: Ukrainian Folk Ballet of the Twin Cities
long_description: The Ukrainian Folk Ballet of the Twin Cities was founded in Minneapolis in 1934 under the direction of Vasile Avramenko. The aims of the group were to organize Ukrainian youth, promote Ukrainian arts and culture, especially the national dances, and to promote the Ukrainian cultural heritage among Americans. Its membership consisted of young people from the parish of St. Michael's Ukrainian Orthodox Church in Minneapolis and included many non-Ukrainians over the years. Records (1934-1953) of the Ukrainian Folk Ballet of the Twin Cities consist of three scrapbooks containing the constitution, programs, newspaper clippings, and photographs. [Finding Aid available at http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4664]

title: Women’s Co-operative Guild (Virginia, Minnesota) Records
long_description: Records (1952-1975) of the Virginia, Minnesota Women's Co-op Guild include two scrapbooks of the organization's activities and of the Virginia area people and events, many of them Finnish related. Also included is a dues and membership notebook and a file of correspondence concerning the summer camp program sponsored by the organization. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4735]

title: Zdenka Rypka Papers
long_description: Zdenka K. (Sojka) Rypka (1894-1975), was born in Washington, Iowa. In 1913 she graduated from John Marshall High School in Chicago, Ill., and became a teacher in the area of Osage and St. Ansgar, Iowa, later moving to Owatonna, Minnesota. During the 1920's, Zdenka was active in the Western Fraternal Life Association (Zapadni Cesko-Bratrska Jednota) and was involved in Czech home talent plays. During the 1930's, she was active as a 4-H Club Leader. The papers of Zdenka Rypka (1894-1975) include family correspondence, diaries and notebooks, photographs, scrapbooks and clippings. The collection also includes her handwritten transcriptions of Czech folk songs, as well as published programs and other material from Czech American fraternal organizations. [Finding Aid available at http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/6/resources/4530]

title: Carver Land Grant Papers
long_description: These papers document the claims made in the early nineteenth century by several individuals upon all or part of a tract of land in present-day Minnesota and Wisconsin, supposedly granted to Jonathan Carver by two Naudowessie Indian chiefs in 1767, centering on claims made by Robert McLenehan and others in 1815-16. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/1]

title: Convento y Hospital de Refugio Records
long_description: The folio is an account book of the Convento y Hospital de Santa Toribio de Refugio de Incurables de la Religión Bethlehemitica de la Ciudad de Lima, beginning in 1723 and ending in 1793. The records contain monthly totals of accounts payable and receivable, and details of monies received from rents and benefactions. Also included are records of patients (often indigent, among them present and former enslaved persons), the length of their stays, and the cost of their treatment and maintenance. Two audits from the Padre Prefecto appear in the folio. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/9]

title: Documenting Jesuit Activity in Mexico and South America
long_description: This massive archive of Jesuit manuscripts documents the relationship between the Jesuits, Spanish authorities, the Indians of South America, and the Portuguese in Brazil in the 17th and 18th centuries. Included are depictions of battles with the Portuguese, discussions of the state of the Jesuit missions, including their commercial activities, the arming of the Indians, descriptions of specific encomiendas and haciendas, the actions of slave raiders, internal Jesuit administrative affairs, operation of Jesuit schools, and documents related to the expulsion of the Jesuits. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/6823]

title: Historical Maps
long_description: The James Ford Bell Library makes history come alive through its collection of maps, rare books, & manuscripts that focus on trade & cross-cultural interaction circa 1800. Our premier collection of more than 25,000 rare books, maps, and manuscripts illustrates the ways in which cultural influences expanded worldwide, with a special emphasis on European interactions. The Bell Library, its collection, and its innovative programs support scholarship and education at all levels, and enrich our community by advancing understanding of this global heritage, making the world we live in more meaningful. The items in the collection currently date between 400 C.E. and 1825 C.E.

title: Izcue y Arias (Firm) Records and Related Documents
long_description: The collection contains eleven bound volumes of manuscript materials dating from the eighteenth century, the early nineteenth century, the Wars of Independence (ca. 1812-1824), and into the initial years of the Republic of Peru. The folios contain the letter books and account books of the Peruvian mercantile house of Izcue y Arias, and an account book of Izcue y Arias business asociate Dr. José Vidal. A separate account of cargo and passengers aboard the ship Divina Pastora, ca. 1799, which carried Izcue freight, is contained in a 12th volume. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/7]

title: James Ford Bell Library General Collection
long_description: Materials from the collections of the University of Minnesota's James Ford Bell Library.

title: Jesuit Manuscripts Relating to China
long_description: This manuscript collection demonstrates the ways in which the Jesuit order attempted to understand and learn the cultural traditions, language, literature, history, and philosophy of the peoples they lived among and attempted to convert. The documents, from the years 1725 through 1732, are heavily oriented towards Jesuit essays on and/or critiques of Chinese treatises on history, astronomy, Confucian philosophy, and science. Some of the documents also deal with the standing of the Jesuits in China at the time, particularly with the relationship between the emperor and the order, which culminated in the expulsion of the Jesuits by Yung Cheng in 1724 and the execution of the Portuguese Jesuit João Morão in 1726 or 1727. Five documents are written in French, three in Latin, and two in Italian. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/5]

title: John Fullerton Papers Concerning the Events at Jeddah, 1727
long_description: On June 6, 1727, six Englishmen were attacked in a riot in Jeddah, while their ship "Prince George" was docked in the port. This collection includes an eyewitness account by the only survivor, John Fullerton, along with related materials. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/9478]

title: John Gabriel Stedman Archive and Book Manuscript
long_description: This collection includes autobiographical sketch covers from 1744-1772 and comprises 32 sheets, inscribed in double columns on both sides, almost all 34 x 42 cm. Diaries include 3 vols., 14-17 cm., which cover: October 29, 1772 to April 29, 1774; January 1, 1778 to January 1, 1779; and May 2, 1794 to June, 1796. Journal comprises 33 sheets of the same size and layout as the sketch, covering October, 1775 to December, 1776; August, 1784 to December, 1787; and sections for parts of May, 1789 to July, 1796. The other papers comprise 53 items, and include correspondence, photographs, copies of military records, etc.

title: John Smith Journals and Papers, 1758-1794
long_description: The 32 pocket memorandum books and acillary documents in this collection capture daily life and agricultural concerns, including trade, of John Smith (1722-1795), a farmer in Gloucester County, England, whose efforts did much to advance agriculture in the county during his lifetime. The collection itself contains no historical information about Smith or his family outside of what can be gleaned from the near-daily entries in the leather-bound diary entries that make up the bulk of the collection. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/8043]

title: Jorunn Selbyg Map Collection
long_description: This collection consists of 88 high quality printed maps of France spanning the years 1757-1899. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/9471]

title: Manuel Gallego y Valcarcel Papers
long_description: The first one hundred and sixty-four documents [Box #1] are letters from and to Gallego. They cover a wide variety of subjects, including Gallego family business, political events and prominent persons in Spain and Argentina, and the challenges of transatlantic commerce. Members of Gallego’s family are prominently featured, especially his brother-in-law Pedro Gomez y Garcia. The correspondence ranges from 1791 to 1806, roughly the last two decades of Spanish imperial rule in the Rio de la Plata. Box #2 contains documents concerning Gallego’s commercial affairs, including his involvement in the slave trade. Part of his post-mortem inventory is also included in the collection. The last two folders contain miscellaneous business from the post-colonial period. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/2483]

title: Spanish American Political Texts
long_description: A selection of Spanish American political text held by the James Ford Bell Library.

title: Swedish East India Company Records
long_description: This collection consists of correspondence and administrative documents from the Swedish East India Company. Documents date between 1698 and 1830, with the bulk of the materials dating between the 1730s and 1770s. Nearly two-thirds of this collection are correspondence documents to Charles Irvine (1693-1771) a successful merchant from Aberdeen, Scotland. Correspondence with James Rose, Mary Irvine, and other merchants are also in this collection. Further administrative materials related to the Company includes shipping documents, accounts and invoices, price lists, and legal documents. Nearly the entire collection is handwritten ink on paper; a few documents are from a printing press. Many of the correspondence includes remnants of or entire wax seals from family or company seals. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/3]

title: The De Mey van Streefkerk Papers
long_description: The documents in this collection pertain almost exclusively to the Surinam possessions of the prominent Dutch De Mey family, and they span the years 1717-1830. They contain information about the extended family and conditions in the plantation colony of Surinam in general, but they are particularly concerned with the family estate, including the plantations of Eghtenveen, Ephrata, Utrecht, Souberg, Klein Marceille, and Groot Marceille. The vast majority of the documents pertain to the core of these holdings, the large plantation of Marceille, which was formerly known as Eghtenveen. The other plantations were generally auxiliaries to Marceille. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/4]

title: Titulos Primordiales
long_description: Records of a sugar plantation in Michoacán Province, Mexico, which was sold to the Jesuit Order in 1629, and sold again to a private owner in the 1780s after the expulsion of the Jesuits from Latin America in 1767. Documents in Purépecha, the language of the Purépecha people in the Michoacán Province of Mexico, deal with earlier claims to the lands by the Tarasco people. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/9469]

title: Venice Online
long_description: Manuscripts from the James Ford Bell Library relating to the city of Venice, documenting its history and importance.

title: Viceroyalty of Peru Records
long_description: The collection contains six bound volumes of manuscript materials from eighteenth and early nineteenth century Peru. The folios pertain to the administration of the Viceroyalty of Peru between 1734 and 1812. Records of royal taxation, the royal tobacco monopoly, and royal oversight of imports and exports are included in the collection. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/8]

title: Village of Horche, Spain Records and Papers
long_description: This collection focuses largely on real estate transactions, testaments, and matters related to censos (investments in local chaplaincies). The real estate acquisitions of José Gallego in the mid-nineteenth century form a significant part of the collection. The collection also contains Spanish government tax documents, village of Horche administrative records, private legal disputes, a defamation case, bills and correspondence from attorneys and notaries, a monastic inventory, and a debt imprisonment case, among others. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/2/resources/6]

title: Annual and Quarterly Reports of YMCA International Work in China
long_description: Annual and quarterly reports of North American YMCA foreign secretaries working in various cities in China between 1895 and 1949. This set of reports was collated from the set of bound Reports of Foreign Secretaries (for all countries) and from the records of YMCA International Work in China. In addition to documenting the successes and challenges of establishing the Young Men's Christian Association in China, the reports provide unique observations on Chinese society during the late Qing and Republican periods. The reports also document the YMCA movement's role in introducing and spreading Western philosophies of education, public health, and physical fitness. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/927]

title: Bedford YMCA Records
long_description: Collected materials from the Bedford Branch of the YMCA of Greater New York, located in Brooklyn. Covers early history and founding, focuses on the 1960s and 1970s with special attention to the Board of Managers and vocational training. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/791]

title: Brooklyn Central YMCA records
long_description: Collected minutes, reports, correspondence, pamphlets, flyers, governing documents, fund raising material, program information and publications primarily from the Brooklyn Central branch of the YMCA of Greater New York. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/833]

title: Butler Street YMCA Records
long_description: Meeting minutes, reports, financial data, program information, and other records of the Butler Street YMCA, which served primarily the African American community of Atlanta from 1894 until 2012. Most of the material consists of the files of DeWitt N. Martin, president and CEO of the Y from 1975 until it closed its doors in 2012. The records include files compiled by Martin as part of his efforts to keep the Butler Street YMCA open despite financial issues and pressure from the national headquarters to close or merge with the Metro Atlanta YMCA. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/790]

title: Carlton Avenue YMCA records
long_description: Included in the Carlton Avenue branch collection are pamphlets and other publicity materials, annual dinner programs, reports related to the closing of the branch and the controversy over the firing of the executive secretary, newsletters and magazines issued by the branch, and information about program attendance and building specifications. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/2487]

title: Causenetic Podcast Records
long_description: This collection includes audio recordings of episodes of the Causenetic podcast created by staff of the YMCA of Metropolitan Dallas from 2019 to 2023. The podcast was focused on expanding the YMCA’s mission to audiences and providing conversation, inspiration, and influence about a variety of timely community topics. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/11496]

title: Channing Tobias Papers
long_description: The papers include news clippings, articles, speeches, correspondence, reports, and other records documenting Tobias's work with the YMCA, the Federal Council of Churches of Christ in America, and other organizations, primarily in the area of race relations. Records of the YMCA's Colored Work Department, of which Tobias was senior secretary from 1923 to 1946, include minutes, correspondence, surveys, reports, and material from several conferences, including the 1923 YMCA Constitutional Convention. Federal Council of Churches material dates from the World War II era and includes minutes, reports, and correspondence relating to that organization's response to racism and other post-war social problems. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/916]

title: Charles K. Ober Papers
long_description: Ober's papers contain a variety of materials relating to his Association work. There is considerable material, primarily correspondence, relating to the student movement. Other materials relate to the recruiting and training of secretaries and correspondence from state committees concerning finances, personnel and conventions. There are also files for each state containing correspondence relating to the work of state committees in matters of finance, personnel and conventions. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/851]

title: Colored Work Department Records
long_description: Reports, correspondence, publications, and other records of the Colored Work Department and predecessor programs, established as avenues for African American participation in and service to the YMCA. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/913]

title: D. Willard Lyon Papers
long_description: Reports, letters, and related papers of YMCA foreign secretary D. Willard Lyon, concerning his work in China and the development of the YMCA movement in China from the late 1890s to the early 1930s. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/8042]

title: Emma Young Dickson Papers
long_description: Correspondence, diaries and other papers of Emma Young Dickson, documenting her service with the YMCA in France during World War I. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/917]

title: Eugene Turner China-related Correspondence
long_description: Correspondence, primarily with Madame Chiang Kai-Shek (Mayling Soong Chiang) concerning reports about and perceptions of the political situation in China, as well as related correspondence with other YMCA colleagues S.C. Leung and Sherwood Eddy. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/7874]

title: Fletcher S. Brockman and Family Papers
long_description: Materials written by and about Fletcher Sims Brockman (1867-1944), who worked for the YMCA in various positions for 37 years. The collection includes correspondence, published material, photographs, a photo album, and other records. A significant portion of the colleciton is comprised of family correspondence written mainly by Brockman’s daughter-in-law Hazel (Iles) Brockman to her parents while she and her husband, Allen Clark Brockman (Fletcher's eldest son), lived abroad in both Hong Kong and Bombay. While neither of the two worked directly for the YMCA, the letters detail different aspects of Hazel’s life throughout time, including some of her volunteer work with the YWCA in each place she lived abroad. Additionally, the collection contains materials regarding biographical and genealogical records of the Brockmans (including Fletcher's two other sons Washington Clark Brockman and Emory Wood Brockman), the memorial service for Fletcher Sims Brockman, both published and unpublished written work by Brockman (including records of his book “I Discover the Orient” and miscellaneous speeches, articles and pamphlets), material from his time working for the YMCA in China, and reports and meeting notes from the Committee for the Promotion of Friendship between America and the Far East, Inc. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/7704]

title: Flushing YMCA Photographs
long_description: This collection includes black and white photographs, primarily 5 x 8 images, of events, buildings and people at the Flushing YMCA in Queens, New York. The collection includes a small number of snapshot-size photographs. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/832]

title: Frank Kiehne Papers
long_description: The Frank Kiehne Papers reflect Kiehne's life long involvement in the YMCA from his experience as a youth program director in Chicago in 1947 to his retirement as the Secretary for Refugees and Rehabilitation for the World Alliance of YMCAs in 1990. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/886]

title: George Jaynes Papers
long_description: The collection consists of the papers of George A. Jaynes, who served the New York City Y in a variety of administrative and financial positions during his 30-year career. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/899]

title: George Williams College Records
long_description: Records documenting the operations, administration, and academic output of George Williams College from its origins in the 1880s to its eventual merger with Aurora University in the mid-1980s, especially including dissertations and theses. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/857]

title: George Williams College Theses and Dissertations
long_description: Theses and dissertations produced by students of George Williams College in partial fulfillment of the requirements for bachelors and masters degrees. Topics include religion and church history, physical education, kinesiology, recreation, social work, group work, youth work, and the YMCA and its history, among others. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/858]

title: Gilbert Beaver Papers
long_description: Materials in this collection include letters and papers about urban social work, student affairs and the relation of church and state. Correspondence with Beaver also includes many letters from YMCA workers abroad concerning both administrative matters and personal experiences. Accounts relate the conditions in China and recount conversations with leaders such as Chiang Kai-Shek. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/875]

title: Harlem YMCA (125th Street) Records
long_description: Collected materials from the 125th Street Harlem Branch covering governance, programming, finance. Also includes historical materials from 1855-1922. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/793]

title: Harlem YMCA (135th Street) records
long_description: The Harlem branch (135th Street) YMCA records consist of the minutes from the Board of Managers (1928-1992, non-inclusive), historical materials, public programs (including the Salute to Black Achievers in Industry dinners, 1971-1989), with limited additional material on fundraising and facilities. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/794]

title: Harlem YMCA Photographs
long_description: Collected photographic images from the Harlem Branch of the YMCA of Greater New York, located on West 135th Street in Manhattan. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/795]

title: Herbert Parker Lansdale, Jr. Papers
long_description: The bulk of the collection is correspondence written by and to Herb and his wife Jessie during their stay in Athens, Greece after Herb's retirement in 1972. Also included are personal materials, including extensive genealogical material, as well as circular letters sent from Athens, which describe the political climate there during the early 1970s. The development of the YMCA in Greece is documented in a series of correspondence and documents collected by Lansdale. The American Farm School in Thessaloniki, Greece, which was headed by Lansdale's son Bruce is also documented in this collection. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/878]

title: International Work Subject Files
long_description: Subject files comprised of correspondence, reports, minutes, memoranda, and printed material concerning various aspects of YMCA work abroad, especially financial issues, boys' work, and war work. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/987]

title: Interracial Programs Records
long_description: Reports, correspondence, and other records documenting various committees, programs, and conferences intended to monitor and promote the process of integration and the elimination of racial inequality within the YMCA, as well as to identify and address the unmet needs of African American and other non-white people served by the organization. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/914]

title: James O. Stephenson Papers
long_description: Correspondence, memos, reports and planning documents collected by James O. Stephenson while he was director of program services at the YMCA of Greater New York. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/6789]

title: Jesse Alexander Papers
long_description: Papers documenting the YMCA career of Jesse N. Alexander, Jr., particularly his work in the area of race relations within the movement and his involvement with the National Conference of Black and Non-White YMCA Staff (BAN-WYS). [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/915]

title: John R. Mott Papers
long_description: The papers include correspondence covering a wide range of YMCA topics: Mott's travels, the administration of foreign and student work, World War I and II relief work, meetings and conferences. Also included are Mott's reports on his travels, especially his 1895-1896 world tour; pamphlets authored by Mott; correspondence concerning the Mott Fellowship Fund, which was established after his death and reports and lists of Mott's papers in other repositories. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/849]

title: Leo Marsh Papers
long_description: Papers of Leo Bergman Marsh, YMCA National Board staff member and leader, documenting his career in the YMCA, which spanned the years from 1928 to 1976. The bulk of the papers concern his extensive work promoting improved race relations within the movement. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/918]

title: Max Yergan Papers
long_description: Papers and files, mainly appearing to have been compiled by the American YMCA's International Committee, concerning Max Yergan, who pioneered YMCA work in South Africa and went on to co-found the Council on African Affairs. Includes correspondence from and about Yergan, reports by Yergan on his work and concerning the situation in South Africa and other African countries, newsletters, news releases, clippings, and various publications. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/7168]

title: McBurney YMCA Records
long_description: Collected minutes, correspondence, reports, fund-raising material, financial records, brochures, correspondence and letter books, statistical and other reports, clippings, and publications, from the McBurney YMCA of Greater New York, located in Manhattan. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/6792]

title: Minneapolis YMCA Camping Services Records
long_description: Records documenting the administration of camping programs of the YMCA of the Greater Twin Cities. Records of camps Icaghowan, Ihduhapi, Menogyn, Warren and various day camps started by the YMCA of Metropolitan Minneapolis are included. Also included are records of camps St. Croix, Widjiwagan, and duNord that were established by the YMCA of Greater St. Paul. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/5898]

title: Minneapolis YMCA General Administrative Records
long_description: Records documenting the administration and evolution of the YMCA of Metropolitan Minneapolis organization, including committee minutes, finances, campaigns, general correspondence, reports, international and World Service activities, programs, and marketing and public relations materials. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/844]

title: Minneapolis YMCA Photographs, Slides, and Audiovisual Materials
long_description: Photographs, slides, and audiovisual materials depicting the buildings, programs, events, and activities of the Minneapolis YMCA. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/845]

title: Miscellaneous New York YMCA Branch Photographs
long_description: The collection of New York YMCA branch photographs includes images from small or short-lived branches as well as small collections from larger branches of the New York YMCA. There are numerous images of YMCA buildings, programs and activities. Most of the photographs are professional, black and white images. [Finding Aid available at: http://purl.umn.edu/53013]

title: Miscellaneous YMCA Research, Planning and Development Records
long_description: Reports, correspondence, publications, minutes, and other records from various YMCA of the USA departments dealing with research and planning. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/869]

title: New York City YMCA Building and Property Records
long_description: The collection includes contracts, inventories, blueprints and designs, bid documents, maintenance schedules, needs assessments, training materials, energy audits, appraisals, insurance policies and other materials related to the buildings and property owned by the YMCA of Greater New York. The bulk of the collection is from the period 1960-1990. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/6146]

title: New York YMCA Annual Reports
long_description: Annual reports of the YMCA of the City of New York, YMCA of Greater New York, Brooklyn Young Men's Christian Association, and Brooklyn and Queens Young Men's Christian Association for the period 1852-2000. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/905]

title: New York YMCA Board of Directors Records
long_description: Collected records of the YMCA of Greater New York Board of Directors and its subcommittees. The materials cover the period from the 1850s to the 2000s. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/855]

title: New York YMCA Photographs
long_description: The New York YMCA photo collection includes images of buildings, events, executives and staff, award recipients, activities, programs, dinners and other miscellaneous subjects photographed by or for the YMCA of Greater New York. Most are black and white professional photographs taken for publicity and marketing purposes. Also included in the collection are negatives (including glass plate negatives), contact sheets, slides, graphics for clothing, snapshots and photoengraving. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/809]

title: New York YMCA Program and Event Records
long_description: The collection includes extensive files on education, job and other training programs operated by the YMCA of Greater New York in the 1960s through 1980s in conjunction with public and private agencies. It also includes materials on athletics, events, international programs, boys and youth work and other aspects of programing at the YMCA of Greater New York from the 1880s into the 21st century. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/6825]

title: New York YMCA Reports, Studies and Surveys
long_description: The collection of New York YMCA reports, studies and surveys includes both association-wide and program and branch level information. For example, there is considerable material about the McBurney School and the William Sloane House branch, which closed in 1988 and 1992 respectively. There are unit cost studies, studies of facilities needs, studies of individual programs and branches, surveys of members and staff, marketing research studies, long-range planning reports, and studies of the YMCA's residential operations. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/7161]

title: Physical Education Program Records
long_description: The Physical Education Program Records contain records of the YMCA's Physical Department, Physical Education Committee, and other governing committees, as well as several of its prominent leaders in this field. Material includes minutes, correspondence, various physical education studies, publications, and convention materials, as well as program materials for various sports and fitness activities, especially scuba diving. Also included are records of related organizations, such as the Physical Education Society and the Athletic League. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/925]

title: Records of Local Young Men's Christian Associations
long_description: Scattered constitutions and by-laws, histories, minutes, reports, correspondence, photographs, newspapers, journals, articles, publicity, building records, surveys, studies, handbooks, and other material associated with the operation and functions of local YMCA associations in North American, particularly Hawaii and Chicago, Illinois, as well as their connection to the national board of the North American YMCA. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/884]

title: Records of the YMCA of the City of New York
long_description: Includes minutes, account books, scrapbooks, ephemera, correspondence, newspaper clippings, brochures and pamphlets, journals, committee reports and other materials that document the early history of the YMCA in New York City. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/6769]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in Bulgaria
long_description: This collection includes correspondence, minutes, reports, financial documents, pamphlets, constitutions, articles and other records of the YMCA movement in Bulgaria, mainly in Sofia. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/970]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in China
long_description: Records documenting YMCA work in China include histories, annual reports, report letters, correspondence, minutes, records of specific programs and activities, building records (including building plans), financial records, biographical records, pamphlets, and maps. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/931]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in Egypt
long_description: Includes correspondence, minutes, reports, financial documents, property records, maps, development plans, pamphlets, newspaper and magazine articles, and other records of the International YMCA movement in Egypt. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/949]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in Estonia
long_description: This collection includes correspondence, minutes, reports, financial documents, development plans, pamphlets, newspaper and magazine articles and other records of YMCA international work in Estonia, especially on refugee relief work, hygiene promotion in children, the organization and administration of a school system for youth and night classes for refugees and returned soldiers, the operation of social and athletic clubs and the joint operation, with the Red Cross, of a large summer camp. Much of the later material involves the Estonian YMCA's move to become autonomous. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/971]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in France
long_description: This collection includes correspondence, minutes, reports, financial documents, pamphlets, maps, journal and newspaper articles and other records documenting YMCA work in France, especially youth and publishing work done in France for Russian refugees. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/967]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in Greece
long_description: Correspondence, minutes, reports, financial documents, development plans, maps, pamphlets, journal and newspaper articles and other records of the YMCA movement in Greece. The main topic of in the collection is the YMCA's civilian work in Greece, primarily in Athens and Thessaloniki (also referred to as Salonica and Saloniki), but war work is also documented. Camps in Salamis, Pelion and Chalkidiki are discussed with prominence as well. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/984]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in Hong Kong
long_description: Correspondence, reports, financial records, and printed material documenting YMCA international work in Hong Kong, including work with both the Chinese and European populations. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/934]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in India
long_description: This collection includes correspondence, reports, pamphlets, maps, financial records, building records, and other material documenting YMCA international work in India, in addition to some records from Burma, Ceylon, and Pakistan. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/959]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in Japan
long_description: The records of the YMCA work in Japan consist of extensive correspondence and reports of the foreign secretaries. Reports, correspondence, and publications of the National Council are also included. Correspondence describing Japanese influences in Korea and China are included as well as local YMCA association records, including reports, correspondence, building records and plans, and pamphlets. Other records documenting the YMCA work include financial records, student records, records of specific programs, histories, pamphlets, periodicals and photos. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/930]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in Korea
long_description: The collection includes correspondence, reports, and printed material from YMCA international work in Korea, particularly the Seoul Association. A significant portion of the records consist of correspondence and documents concerning the financial campaigns and building projects of the Korean YMCAs, but also includes information on Korean-Japanese relations, physical education, rural work, and student work, as well as scattered correspondence describing political events in Korea. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/948]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in Palestine and Israel
long_description: Correspondence, minutes, reports, financial records, architectural data and drawings, audio recordings, printed material, and other records of the work of the American YMCA movement in Palestine and Israel. The bulk of the files concern Jerusalem, with particularly rich documentation on the the construction of the YMCA's landmark West Jerusalem (Jerusalem International YMCA) building. Also included in the records are files concerning YMCA work in other areas of the region, especially East Jerusalem, as well as Peniel-by-Galilee, Nazareth, and other locales. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/929]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in Poland
long_description: This collection includes correspondence, minutes, reports, financial documents, music books, pamphlets, maps, photographs, journal and newspaper articles and other records of the YMCA movement in Poland, mostly focusing on the work of Paul Super on building projects and the state of Poland and Polish groups in exile after both German and Soviet occupation. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/969]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in Russia and the Soviet Union
long_description: Records of YMCA work in Russia and the Soviet Union consisting primarily of correspondence among YMCA secretaries working in Russia, as well as correspondence and reports to YMCA leaders in the Unites States on matters relating to programs, relations with the Orthodox Church, finances, membership recruitment, and work with World War I soldiers and prisoners of war. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/928]

title: Records of YMCA International Work in the Philippines
long_description: Correspondence, reports, financial and property records, and printed material documenting YMCA international work in the Philippines, including material on local associations, Army-Navy work, and rural reconstruction. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/940]

title: Records of YMCA Work in England and the United Kingdom
long_description: Correspondence, minutes, reports, financial documents, pamphlets, journal and newspaper articles and other records concerning the YMCA movement in England. Early records include the development of United Kingdom YMCAs. English, Scottish, Welsh and Irish national council reports and yearbooks, reports and other records from local associations, as well as material related to the YMCA's role during World War I and II make up the bulk of this material. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/979]

title: Records of YMCA Work with American Indians
long_description: Reports, correspondence, newsletters, and historical material regarding YMCA work with indigenous people in the United States, particularly the Dakota Indians in South Dakota and Nebraska. Much of the collection consists of historical files compiling early correspondence, reports, articles, and constitutions, along with summaries of events prepared by various YMCA historians and librarians. Also included in the collection are records concerning several of the Indian schools and YMCA Indian summer schools, especially the schools in Carson, Nevada and Carlisle, Pennsylvania, as well as Riggs Institute in Flandreau, South Dakota, and small amounts of material from or about various Native American YMCA branches in South Dakota. The collection also includes several newsletters, including one in the Dakota language. Material from the 1970s and later consists primarily of records of the Sioux Young Men's Christian Association and its relationship with the YMCA's World Service division, including material collected and donated by Daryl Soltau, a board of trustees member of the General Convention of Sioux YMCAs. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/996]

title: Records of YMCA Work with Women, Girls, and Families
long_description: Correspondence, minutes, reports, financial documents, pamphlets, journal and newspaper articles, scrapbooks, studies and other records documenting North American YMCA’s programs for and policies regarding women, girls and families. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/894]

title: Richard C. Morse Papers
long_description: Papers of Morse's fifty year tenure as general secretary with the YMCA. Includes information on the Morse family genealogy. Morse's papers include a variety of materials relating to the International Committee of the YMCA: correspondence relating to personnel; reports and speeches on "colored work," the growth of the YMCA, secretaryship of the YMCA and the International Committee itself. There is also material relating to Morse's interest in the association at Yale University and the construction of Dwight Hall. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/860]

title: Richard D. Cooper China Diary and Other Papers
long_description: Diary describing Cooper and his family's travel to China and his work there with the YMCA. Also includes a few report letters from his subsequent work in India and Sri Lanka during the 1950s and 1960s. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/8044]

title: Robert McBurney Papers
long_description: The papers include biographical sketches, articles and reminiscences. There are also two lengthy biographical manuscripts, one by L. L. Doggett and one by John Morse. Also included are papers and addresses by McBurney on a variety of topics. Correspondence regarding local and national administrative matters with Thomas Cree, William Dodge, Richard Morse, Dwight Moody and other YMCA leaders can be found in this collection. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/877]

title: Russell N. Service Papers
long_description: The Russell N. Service collection consists of minutes and printed matter from several organizations, especially the Federation of Concerned Associations (FOCA), formed in 1967. FOCA was made up of black and white executives from more than a dozen northeastern inner city YMCAs in an effort to deal with the problems of the urban core in large cities served by these YMCAs. In particular, FOCA was formed to address the gap between professed policy and practice, the lack of urgency about the problems of the inner cities, and the inadequate involvement of black YMCA professionals and laypeople in developing solutions. Russell Service served on the Executive Committee of the organization and was also acting chairman and chairman. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/900]

title: State, Regional, National and International YMCA records of Greater NY
long_description: Minutes, agendas, brochures and pamphlets, correspondence, proceedings, committee reports, publications and journals, and other materials that reflect the involvement of the YMCA in New York City in state, regional, national and international YMCA organizations. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/7174]

title: Student Work Records
long_description: Minutes, correspondence, reports, topical files, publications, and other material documenting the work of the YMCA with students on college and university campuses in the United States and Canada. Also included are records concerning other national and international Christian student groups with which the Student YMCA worked. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/998]

title: Trench and Camp Newspaper
long_description: Camp Cody (Deming, New Mexico) was one of thirty different editions of Trench and Camp newspaper published by the YMCA's National War Work Council for various U.S. Army camps. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/882]

title: Trench and Camp Newspaper
long_description: A nearly complete run of the Camp Upton (Long Island, N.Y.) edition of Trench and Camp, a newspaper published by the National War Work Council of the YMCA, in partnership with various city newspapers, for soldiers during WWI. The paper was printed in different editions for each of the many camps, with about half the material supplied weekly from a central editorial office, and half by local reporters. Its purpose was “to print the news, to inform, to stimulate, and to help relieve the tedium and monotony of camp life” for soldiers, as well as “to be a graphic account of the life of our soldiers, whether they be drilling or fighting, at home or ‘over there’” for civilians. In addition, each Trench and Camp was a channel of communication to the troops from the President, Congress, and War Department. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/882]

title: United Service Organizations-Related Records
long_description: Materials in this collection include club histories and photographs of both Army/Navy and industrial USOs, administrative files, information on associated organizations, miscellaneous records of individual USO clubs, and print materials.
