long_description: Archive collection of the German archaeologist's work, focusing mainly on the 1929-1932 excavations in the ancient Parthian and Sassanian city of Ktesiphon (Ctesiphon), now in modern day Iraq, but containing material through 1938

long_description: Images from the ballooning collections--Scholl, Winzen, and Piccard--held by the University of Minnesota's Special Collections and Rare Books.

long_description: A collection of individual manuscript leaves held by the Special Collections & Rare Books unit of the University of Minnesota Libraries and housed in the Elmer L. Andersen Library.

title: Joseph S. Mertle Collection on the History of Photomechanics
long_description: The Mertle Collection contains original books, journals, photographs, and manuscripts relating to photographic processes in printing from the early period to the middle of the twentieth century. The collection includes approximately 6,000 books, plus more than 1,000 artifacts and non-print items. Noteworthy items in the collection include the technical possessions and specimen reproductions made by Karel Klic, world-renowned inventor of rotogravure; the business records and correspondence of Max Levy, pioneer manufacturer of halftone screens; the private correspondence and personal effects of the American photohistorian, Edward Epstean; and the personally executed sketches of dot formations and technical data complied by halftone researcher Arthur Fruwith.

title: Maywald Collection
long_description:
The inclusion of intricate initial capitals at the beginning of a paragraph was common in medieval manuscripts as early as the 7th century CE. Scribes would frequently add decorative illustrated letters to embellish the page. That tradition carried on after Johannes Gutenberg’s invention of printing using metal type and a printing press in Europe in 1439. Rather than hand illustrating each capital, printers carved decorative letters in wood and composed them in the press with metal type to replicate the scribe’s hand-drawn art.

The resulting letterforms were so striking that collectors often cut them out of books and manuscripts during the late 19th century. Dr. Claus Maywald, head librarian at the Gutenberg Museum in Mainz, Germany, assembled over 6,000 examples of these initials that had been removed from books and donated this important collection to the University of Minnesota’s Andersen Library in 2011.

The Maywald Collection includes ornamental initials from 1470 to 1690, books containing exemplar initials, and contemporary reproductions created using modern technology and printed using traditional letterpress methods. These initial letterform styles include:

  • Floriated — With plant and/or flower motifs
  • Historiated — With people or places from a specific story
  • Inhabited — With people, mythical beings, or faces
  • Speaking — Representing the first letter of the subject, i.e. C for Cecelia
  • Zoomorphic — With animals
  • Criblée — With a stippled dot pattern in the background
  • Calligraphic — Representing the stroke of the flat-nibbed pen
  • Ornamental — Decoration that is nonrepresentational.

These letterforms reveal the unparalleled craftsmanship and imagination of wood engravers who created wood type for use in early printing. The detail achieved by the carvers was done mostly without magnification and using only natural light. Many of these letters are no larger than postage stamps and the skill required to do this (backwards and in relief) is extraordinary.

title: Michael L. Courtney Papers
long_description: The collection includes Illinois Volunteer Infantry and United States Army commissions awarded for gallantry in the Civil War, a law degree from Columbia University, and a wedding invitation.

title: Miscellaneous Manuscripts Collection
long_description: This collection includes manuscripts, account books, ships' journals, travel diaries, government manuscripts, journals, etc. purchased by Library staff and consolidated in one collection.

title: Papyri and Ostraka Collection
long_description: The University of Minnesota's collection of documents from ancient Egypt consists of twenty-one fragments of papyri written in Greek, one fragment written in Egyptian hieroglyphic script, and two ostraka, one in Greek, the other in demotic Egyptian.

title: Photochrom Collection
long_description: Photochroms prints are colorized images produced from black-and-white photographic negatives via the direct photographic transfer of a negative onto lithographic printing plates. The process is a photographic variant of chromolithography, a broader term that refers to color lithography in general. These images come from a number of photochrom collections held in Special Collections and Rare Books.

title: Postcard Collection
long_description: A collection of historical postcards held in the University of Minnesota's Special Collections and Rare Books.

title: Rare Books and Manuscripts
long_description: The Special Collections, Rare Books, and Manuscripts (SCRBM) unit serves as the repository for University Libraries materials that require special protection because of their age, value or fragility. These holdings include clay tablets and papyri, medieval manuscripts, early printed books, miniature books, fine printing and fine bindings. Presented here are materials from the general rare book and manuscript collections.

title: Theaterwork & Gathering Post
long_description: Theaterwork was a journal that began in the 1980s in St Peter, MN. It emerged from the Cherry Creek Theatre group, which organized in the 1970s along with the founding of the El Teatro Laboratorio. While the journal only lasted two years, the content documented a furtive period of community-based theater that focused on human rights issues, the environment, and diversity as well as international intersections in performance and puppetry, playwriting, productions, national festivals, and workshops. The Gathering Post was a newspaper also begun in St Peter, MN, around the same time as Theaterwork, and in tandem with the work of the Cherry Creek Theater. Like Theaterwork, but less formal, the newspaper served to connect community and the arts.

title: World War Materials (Miscellaneous)
long_description: The collection contains recruiting and promotional materials, cartoons, pamphlets, and posters from the United States, France, England, and other countries from the two World Wars plus some German identity papers and other miscellaneous items from that time period.

title: World War One Pamphlet Collection
long_description: The pamphlets treat a broad spectrum of subjects: war, peace, social, political and ethical issues, economic and military concerns, legislation, relief organizations, army training, returning veterans, neutrality. These pamphlets were published worldwide, in all the major languages of the world. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/12/resources/5882]

title: World War Poster Collection
long_description: Posters are from World Wars I and II and the German election of 1932. War posters are from U.S., Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Latin America, and Scandinavia. Subjects include recruiting, war bond sales, food conservation, civil defense and many other topics. Includes war posters from the collections of the Hennepin County Library.

title: AIDS Poster Collection
long_description: The posters presented here represent a global sampling of materials and posters produced concerning the HIV/AIDS crisis. Many of the posters were created as part of different prevention/awareness programs and distributed between the mid-1980s and the mid-1990s. Although most materials relate in some way to the LGBT community - there are posters addressing issues of HIV/AIDS for a number of different communities and from different perspectives. Among the most common issues addressed are: safer sex practices, condom use, information distribution, respect (of oneself and one's partner) and risks associated with drug use.

title: Allan Spear Papers
long_description: The collection contains personal and professional correspondence, news articles, newsletters, campaign materials, photographs, films, publications, diaries, planners, awards, buttons and personal materials of Allan Spear, documenting Spear's early years, career as a faculty member in the History Department at the University of Minnesota, and as a state senator and gay politician in Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/2023]

title: BiCities! T.V.
long_description: Started in 2002, BiCities is the world's longest running show on bisexuality. Hosts Dr. Margaret Charmoli and Dr. Anita Kozan conduct weekly interviews with leading experts and influential members of the bisexual community. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/6824]

title: Catherine Azora-Minda Audio Tapes
long_description: The Catherine Azora-Minda Audio Tapes features recordings of the KFAI radio programs to which she contributed (such as "We Want You To Know" and Womenfolk,") as well as WINGS materials, recordings of "Young Lesbians," and commercially distributed music by lesbian artists (including KD Lang and the Indigo Girls). [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/2137]

title: Chris Cinque Papers
long_description: This collection contains materials donated by Cinque and largely pertain to Cinque’s 20 years of theater work. Materials in this collection were created between 1986-1994, or are undated. Highlights from this collection include: documentation of performances by Cinque across 5 different digital formats, drafts of unpublished/unproduced plays The Marauders and White House Wives, a CD containing a radio production of Growing Up Queer in America, and an annotated script for Toklas, MN by Barrie Borich, Chris Cinque, Randa Downs, and Judith Katz. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/9183]

title: Ed Varga and Minneapolis Homocore Collection
long_description: This collection contains audio and video materials digitized in 2020 and 2021 under a post-custodial agreement with Wisconsin-born trans punk musician and promoter Ed Varga. These recordings document the Minneapolis homocore scene of the late 20th and early 21st centuries, with a focus on events and interviews organized by Varga. More materials related to Varga’s life and work are held in Varga’s papers in the Tretter Collection. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/9467]

title: Eleanor Savage Papers
long_description: Papers, including audiovisual materials, from the Eleanor Savage collection held in the Jean Nickolaus Tretter Collection in GLBT Studies. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/9486]

title: Fresh Fruit Radio Show, KFAI
long_description: This collection contains audio recordings of the Fresh Fruit radio show, as broadcast on Minneapolis's radio station KFAI, 90.3 FM. Hosts include Claude Peck, Gary Peterson, and John Sutton. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/6843]

title: GAZE TV Collection
long_description: The GAZE Television show was a cable access show aired in the Twin Cities. Raw footage includes unedited interviews with Vito Russo, Susan Kimberly, Sharon Kowalski and other national and local leaders of note. Events include unedited footage of Pride Parades, national conferences held in the Twin Cities, the AIDS Quilt on display at the Metrodome, ACT Up protests, memorials and other community events. Between tapes of the shows and the raw footage of interviews and community events, we have a substantive collection of video material that documents the Twin Cities GLBT community in the late 20th century. This collection comprises digitized content from VHS tapes donated to the Tretter Collection in GLBT Studies by Minnesotan publisher, producer, and DJ Brad Theissen. The bulk of the video files are recorded episodes of GAZE-TV, a local Twin Cities area public access cable TV show that aired news and information for LGBT viewers, their family, and their friends. GAZE-TV premiered in 1986, and was later known as Green And Yellow TV (1992-1995), and finally GLBT-TV (2002-2004). Also included among the video files is raw footage from the aforementioned programs, alongside select episodes of other public access cable TV shows that focused on LGBTQ+ communities across the United States. Key subject areas include the HIV/AIDS crisis, arts & entertainment, religion, local and national politics, and extensive news coverage of community events and resources. [Finding Aid available at:https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/7573]

title: GLBT Pride Poster Collection
long_description: GLBT pride posters from across the state of Minnesota, circa 1974 through 2006.

title: HIV-AIDS Caregivers Oral History Project
long_description:
The HIV/AIDS Caregivers Oral History Project seeks to document the HIV/AIDS crisis in the Twin Cities from the 1980s-2000s. The collection contains taped interviews with individuals who worked to provide services to HIV+ people and people with AIDS in Minnesota during these years, as well as written interview transcripts and supporting documentation. Interviews were conducted in two phases over the course of three years (2013-2016). Participants included: Linda Brandt, Sharon Day, Brian Goodroad, Dr. Keith Henry, Sister Joanne Lucid, James Maurer, Dr. Michael Osterholm, Dr. Frank Rhame, Lorraine Teel, Rob Yaeger, Roxanne Anderson, Dr. Jason Baker, Scott Bilodeau, Dr. Peter Carr, Jonathan Hanft, Dr. Laura Hoyt, Juan Jackson, Joe Larson, Clint Lende, Lee Lewis, Nick Metcalf, Ephraim Olani, Chuck Peterson, Sue Purchase, Dr. Miguel Ruiz, Karin Sabey, Dr. Ronald Schut, Sarah Senseman, Dr. Alvine Siaka, Bob Tracy, Gwen Velez, Chris Waller, Kevin Winge, and Dr. Monica Yugu.

The project's core team included: Emil Angelica (Project Manager), Dr. Peter Carr (Public Health Advisor), Barbara W. Sommer (Oral Historian), Andrea Klein Bergman (Researcher and Report Creator), and Jada Hansen. It was sponsored by the Ramsey County Historical Society and was made possible by Legacy funding from the Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund established by the vote of Minnesotans on November 4, 2008, and administered by the Minnesota Historical Society. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/2123]

title: It’s Time Minnesota Records
long_description: The It’s Time Minnesota records are composed of publications, flyers, posters, brochures, circulars, event records, newsletters, clippings, articles, correspondence, political documents, and resource documents used by the It’s Time Minnesota and It’s Time Again Minnesota organization. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/2054]

title: Juliana Hu Pegues Papers
long_description: This collection documents the life and worlds of Juliana Hu Pegues, a queer Asian American artist, activist, and scholar from Juneau, Alaska, who made a Minneapolis her home for several decades in the late 20th and early 21st centuries. The collection focuses on her involvement with Minneapolis-based arts, activist, and LGBTQ organizations from the 1990s to the early 2000s, and include organizational notes, correspondence, books and zines, event press and publicity, radio programs and other audio recordings, political posters and t-shirts, photographs, play scripts, and video recordings of solo and collaborative performances. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/9483]

title: March on Washington Records
long_description: The March on Washington records document the planning and public reception of the 1979, 1987, 1993, and 2000 Gay Rights Marches held in Washington, D.C. The records consist of newsletters, newspaper clippings and articles, VHS tapes, DVDs, promotional flyers, general mailings, planning notes, meeting minutes, and ephemera including a stamp, T-shirts worn to the Marches or distributed at the Marches, and a bracelet. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/2073]

title: Minnesota Men of Color (MMC) Records
long_description: The collection contains administrative records, correspondence, newsletters, reports and articles, educational materials and project and program records created by and concerning the Minnesota Men of Color. MMC promotes awareness and support of HIV/AIDS concerns within the gay men of color communities. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/2102]

title: Minnesota Pandemic Oral History Project
long_description: The Minnesota Pandemic Oral History Project was conducted in 2021 to document information about the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota. The project was funded by a grant from the Minnesota Historical Society and its Minnesota Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund (Legacy fund) to Portal Research of Minneapolis. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/9579]

title: Minnesota-based LGBTQ Periodicals
long_description: This collection consists of newspapers, magazines, and other periodicals published by and for the LGBTQ community in both the Twin Cities and greater Minnesota.

title: Records of ReconcilingWorks - Lutherans for Full Participation
long_description: This collection contains materials from ReconcilingWorks: Lutherans for Full Participation, a national organization founded in 1974 that supports LGBTQ individuals in the Lutheran Church. Included are typed and handwritten sermon notes from several ReconcilingWorks-affiliated pastors, as well as the group’s newsletter, Concord. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/9270]

title: Select Committee for Lesbian, Gay and Bisexual Concerns Records
long_description: The collection contains materials from the Committee relating to their work, mainly during the years from 1992 to 1993. Included are memos to the committee, research materials (including interviews, surveys, and related materials from other Big Ten and CIC universities), materials relating to committee reports, copies of the interim and final committee reports, and materials relating to domestic partner benefits. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/2005]

title: Tretter Audio and Video Inventory
long_description: The Tretter Audio and Visual Inventory is an inventory of all known and discoverable audio and visual materials across multiple collections. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/7384]

title: Tretter General Collection
long_description: Materials from the University of Minnesota's Tretter Collection in Gay, Lesbian, Bisexual and Transgender Studies general collection.

title: Tretter Transgender Oral History Project
long_description:
The Tretter Transgender Oral History Project (TTOHP) collects, preserves, and makes accessible oral histories of gender transgression, especially as theyintersect with race, age, sexuality, citizenship, class, and ability. The project seeks to document the power and vision of trans movements for justice through the stories of activists working to imagine another world.

The first phase of the Tretter Transgender Oral History Project was led by poet and activist Andrea Jenkins—who became the first Black transgender woman to serve in office in the US after she was elected, in 2017, to the Minneapolis City Council. This phase of the project sought to document the life stories and experiences of transgender and gender non-conforming people, with a focus on people living in the upper Midwest as well as those often excluded from the historical record, including trans people of color and trans elders.

The second phase of the Tretter Transgender Oral History Project is led by trans studies scholar Myrl Beam. This phase of work seeks to document histories of trans activist movements and politics in the US, and is grounded in the belief that trans movements for justice are about more than rights: they are about survival, and about creating a new, more fabulous, more livable, and more expansive world––one not structured by racialized gender norms. The oral histories collected during this phase document the transformative power of trans movements, and the stories of trans activists who are building them.

For more about the project, visit: https://www.lib.umn.edu/tretter/transgender-oral-history-project.

title: Twin Cities (TC) Pride Records
long_description: The Twin Cities (TC) Pride Records, 1973-2014 includes the administrative, financial, marketing, and donor materials of Twin Cities Pride. In addition, a substantial collection of memorabilia, event signage, and banners are included within the collection. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/2002]

title: Wally Swan Papers
long_description: The collection contains the personal and professional papers of Wally Swan from 1971-2007. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/13/resources/2088]

title: Arthur E. Schneider Papers
long_description: Contains diaries, photographs, and clippings regarding Arthur E. Schneider's on-site project administration at Seoul National University. Also contains personal materials of Dr. Schneider, professor of forestry at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1753]

title: Bell Museum of Natural History Negatives
long_description: This collection contains departmental records, reports, correspondence, publications, and scrapbooks of the Bell Museum of Natural History at the University of Minnesota. The materials primarily center around the period with Dr. Thomas Sadler Roberts served as director (1915-1946), but also includes items from Dr. Walter Breckenridge's tenure. Because of Dr. Robert's long relationship with the Bell Museum, the collection also contains some of his personal papers. The collection also contains records about the museum's public education programs as well as publications, exhibit catalogues, and posters for exhibitions. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1730]

title: Bell Museum of Natural History Records
long_description: This collection contains departmental records, reports, correspondence, publications, and scrapbooks of the Bell Museum of Natural History at the University of Minnesota. The materials primarily center around the period with Dr. Thomas Sadler Roberts served as director (1915-1946), but also includes items from Dr. Walter Breckenridge's tenure. Because of Dr. Robert's long relationship with the Bell Museum, the collection also contains some of his personal papers. The collection also contains records about the museum's public education programs as well as publications, exhibit catalogues, and posters for exhibitions. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1730]

title: Bisbila University High School Yearbook
long_description: Collection contains records pertaining to University High School at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1298]

title: Board of Regents Supplements
long_description: Supplementary material relating to the University of Minnesota's Board of Regents. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/6862]

title: Campus Maps and Blueprints
long_description: Historical campus maps and blueprints of the University of Minnesota held in the collections of the University of Minnesota Archives.

title: Central Files Records
long_description: Central Files served as an early records management system for the University of Minnesota. The office maintained the University's legal, building, and funding files, along with information regarding the Board of Regents, educational programs and departments, reports of studies carried out, and miscellaneous materials regarding the activities of the departments and administration of the University. Collection contains the records collected by Central Files at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1678]

title: Cereal Rust Laboratory Records
long_description: The Cereal Rust Laboratory Records are composed of materials generated through research and field work performed in four areas : Barberry eradication, rust epidemiology investigations, rust race studies, and rust nursery work. Materials include correspondence, memos, ledgers, reports, studies, publications; brochures and program publicity, instructional materials, news clippings, scrapbooks, photographs and slides. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1018]

title: Chicano Studies Records
long_description: This collection contains correspondence, reports, and proposals for the Chicano Studies Department as well as other Chicano student resources, centers, and organizations. It also contains notes, manuscripts, and clippings from University of Minnesota Chicano faculty. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/7584]

title: Christopher Webber Hall Papers
long_description: The collection consists of the papers of Christopher Webber Hall, professor of geology, mineralogy and biology at the University of Minnesota. His field notebooks contain information about his work as a field geologist, the areas through which he passed, and some comment on traveling and social conditions encountered in the field. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1454]

title: Clarence E. Lund Papers
long_description: Collection contains the papers of Clarence E. Lund, professor emeritus of mechanical engineering at the University of Minnesota. Includes research projects, miscellaneous reports and papers regarding the symposium on preservation for mobilization requirements held at Seoul (Korea) National University in 1956. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1229]

title: Cloquet Forestry Center Records
long_description: The collection consists of the records of the Cloquet Forestry Center during the administrations of William H. Kenety (1912-1921), G.H. Wiggin (1921-1923) and Theodore Schantz-Hansen (1923-1960). [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1262]

title: Clyde H. Bailey Papers
long_description: The collection consists of correspondence, reports, talks, writings, biographical material, and diaries. The collection is arranged in two series: Seoul National University and Subject Files. The Seoul University series covers a period from 1954-1962, when the University underwent rebuilding after the end of the Korean War and Bailey served as a consultant for the agricultural program. The Subject Files series is arranged alphabetically, and includes general correspondence and professional and personal correspondence with professional associations, research institutes, and academic colleagues. Inclusive dates for the subject series are 1911-1965. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1725]

title: College of Agriculture Records
long_description: Collection contains reports, minutes, personal and professional correspondence, letter books, memos, circulars, research synopses, publications, photographs, historical materials, planning documents, financial materials, program reviews and self-studies, surveys, news clippings, scrapbooks, journals, field notebooks, biographies, interview transcripts, time books and property inventories of the various agricultural administrative units at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1656]

title: College of Liberal Arts Records
long_description: This collection contains corresponedence, committee meeting minutes, adminstrative documents, and policies, reports regarding the administration, governing bodies, academic programs, faculty and staff, and students of the College of Liberal Arts, formerly the College of Science, Literature, and the Arts. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/7672]

title: Corn Tassel Southern School of Agriculture Yearbooks
long_description: Part of the Southern School of Agriculture records, the collection contains yearbooks, correspondence, reports, notes, minutes, and agendas that document the administrative and student activities of the Southern School of Agriculture. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1126]

title: Daniel W. Sprague
long_description: This collection contains the papers of Daniel W. Sprague, accountant and recorder at the University of Minnesota from 1887-1890. Included here are financial reports, address on the University of Minnesota, reports from various departmental directors, land grants history. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/5861]

title: Department of African and African American Studies Records
long_description: The collection contains administrative materials regarding the founding and activities of the Department of African and African American Studies at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1599]

title: Department of Botany Print Photograph Collection
long_description: The photograph collections contain thousands of images that document Minnesota landscapes and botanical specimens from the late 1890s to the mid-1940s. Detailed descriptions of these collections can be found in the contents list. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1673]

title: Department of Botany Records
long_description: The collection contains the correspondence files, field notebooks, and various reports for the Department of Botany at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1673]

title: Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences Records
long_description: Collection contains the records of the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1677]

title: Department of Plant Pathology and Physiology Records
long_description: The collection includes student papers from the 1920s though the 1970s, departmental publications, materials relating to St Paul campus building projects, biographical materials on faculty members, and a significant collection of photographs from the early years of the department through the 1980s. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1720]

title: Department of Political Science Records
long_description: The Department of Political Science records contains five series of material that illustrate the work that the department has created at the University of Minnesota from 1823 to 1988. This includes historical material, detailing the founding of the department from 1912 to 1972, meeting minutes and memos from 1925 to 1985, as well as, correspondence organized by date and subject. Other material includes papers on the sub-topic committee, “Civil Liberty in the United States” under the Works Project Administration Project (WPA), from 1920 to 1932, and papers involving the department’s inclusion on the Seoul National University of Korea Cooperative Project, from 1957 to 1962. This collection also holds a number of suject files that illustrate topics of related interest and are organized alphabetically. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1646]

title: Dight Institute Records
long_description: Collection contains the records of the Dight Institute, established at the University of Minnesota in 1941 with a bequest from Charles Fremont Dight. Its mission was to support the study and promulgation of human genetics, provide instruction in human genetics, and establish a resource center for persons who desire counseling on such questions. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1698]

title: Donald Buermann Lawrence Papers
long_description: The Papers of Donald Buermann Lawrence are largely related to glaciological expeditions to South America, 1958-1959, 1967, New Zealand, 1964-1965, 1969, Glacier Bay Alaska, 1941-1988 and the ice fields of Juneau, Alaska, 1949, 1955. There is material also relating to an expedition he made in 1932 to the Jamaican Rain Forest while he was a graduate student at Johns Hopkins University. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1702]

title: Elvin C. Stakman Papers
long_description: The collection documents the life and career of Elvin Charles Stakman, noted plant pathologist, teacher and international agricultural advisor. Of particular interest is the extensive collection of field notes, reports, correspondence, colored maps and photos of wheat rust research and the resultant barberry eradication efforts Stakman lead pre- and post- WWI; teaching materials from Stakman’s career as professor of plant pathology at the University of Minnesota, including seminar notes, student papers and tributes, and bibliographies; and extensive correspondence with plant scientists associated through the Rockefeller Foundation with the “Green Revolution” and with students and agricultural scientists in business and the academy. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1744]

title: Evergreen North Central School of Agriculture Yearbooks
long_description: Part of the North Central Experiment Station records, the collection consists primarily of correspondence, as well as publications and scrapbooks related to the history and operations of the North Central Experiment Station and high school. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1096]

title: Florence J. Julian Papers
long_description: The collection contains nursing and University Hospital administration guides, annual reports, articles and other information about the Variety Club Heart Hospital, correspondence, and a final report on nursing service and education at Seoul National University. Florence Julian was a professor emeritus of nursing and director of nursing at University hospital. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1234]

title: Forrest O. Wiggins Papers
long_description: Collection contains materials regarding the termination of Forrest O. Wiggins from the philosophy faculty at the University of Minnesota. The diverse opinions represented in statements, newspaper accounts and correspondence, all reflect the controversy that surrounded the Wiggins Case. The issues of race, academic freedom, the conservative political climate of the McCarthy Era, the Legislature's supposed interference in University matters, and accusations of poor newspaper reporting based on alleged misquotes by the press, all played a role in the controversy, and are documented in the collection. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1692]

title: Frederick R. Weisman Art Museum Records
long_description: The Frederick R. Weisman Art Museum collection contains the administrative records of the museum as it was known under the following official titles: University Art Gallery (or University Gallery) (1934-1983), University Art Museum (1983-1993), and Frederick R. Weisman Art Museum (1993-present). [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1017]

title: Gaylord W. Anderson Papers
long_description: This collection consists of materials regarding Gaylord Anderson's expertise in epidemiology and communicable diseases. The papers cover the topics of polio, tuberculosis, small pox, rubella, malaria, diphtheria and other diseases. The papers also include correspondence, book proofs, articles, notes, information regarding his military service and retirement, letters, research data, and documents Dr. Anderson's involvement with Seoul National University in the 1950s. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1075]

title: General College Records
long_description: This collection contains the administrative files of General College at the University of Minnesota. The materials include general correspondence, reports, faculty meeting minutes, assembly minutes, committee reports and papers, speeches, institutional research papers, comprehensive examinations, curriculum and course descriptions, enrollment statistics, executive council minutes, articles and correspondence of staff and faculty of General College, college policies, projects and programs participated in by the college and financial records. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1090]

title: Gisela Konopka Papers
long_description: The collection contains both the personal and professional papers of Gisela Konopka. There are extensive speech and correspondence files, as well as writings, teaching materials, biographical materials, and files covering her project on adolescent girls in conflict. There is quite a bit of overlap between series, as well as within particular series. Konopka was involved extensively with various groups and organizations, sometimes consulting and other times giving a talk or writing a paper. She maintained different groupings of files depending on which activity she carried out. She also sent some materials to University Archives, especially speech files, individually, and then later sent another copy as part of a larger run of files. Some of these duplicates were found and brought together during processing, others were not. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1734]

title: Graduate School Records
long_description: The collections contain minutes of committees of the Graduate School, general correspondence, alphabetical files, reports, committee papers, departmental papers, research materials and information regarding various educational societies. The bulk of the material of collection 2007-04 includes materials from 1990-2002, with a small amount of material from the 1980s. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1664]

title: Guillermo C. Rojas Papers
long_description: This collection contains papers of Guillermo Rojas, Chair of Chicano Studies from 1983-2003 at the University of Minnesota. It includes personal materials (research notes, correspondence, etc.) as well as documents related to the Chicano Studies department at UMN. Of note are chronologies of the development of the department and documents of ongoing efforts to sustain it. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/10534]

title: Harold Macy Papers
long_description: The Harold Macy papers consist of correspondence, reports, talks and writings and historical materials generated during Macy’s college years as a student at Cornell University through his years of service to the University of Minnesota as professor, agricultural experiment station director and dean of the Institute of Agriculture. The collection is composed primarily of professional correspondence and talks that Macy gave based on his research interests, principally the use of technology in mold prevention in dairy products. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1218]

title: Helen Hart Papers
long_description: The collection contains reports, charts, and maps related to Dr. Hart's research on plant rusts. It is primarily in the form of annual reports summarizing rust spore data across the United States. The data appears to have been collected as field notes for over three decades by F.E. Haglund, and transferred by Hart first to a paper draft, and then to typescript. Dates covered are primarily for the 1920s and 1930s, with some data for the 1950s, and little for the 1940s. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1172]

title: Helmut G. Heinrich Papers
long_description: The collection documents the professional career of Dr. Helmut G. Heinrich, noted aerospace engineer, parachute technology researcher, and professor at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1276]

title: Henry Francis Nachtrieb Papers
long_description: Nachtrieb’s professional correspondence constitutes the administrative records that document the early history of the Bell Museum of Natural History. As director of the museum, then known as the Zoological Museum, in concurrence with his role as chair of the department of Animal Biology and position as State Zoologist for the Minnesota Geological and Natural History Survey (MGNHS), the incoming and outgoing correspondence in this series documents the activities of the museum prior to and in conjunction with the appointment of Thomas Sadler Roberts as Associate Curator in 1915. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1642]

title: Information Files Collection
long_description: The information files contain newspaper clippings, press releases, magazine articles, newsletters, curriculum vitae, and programs highlighting the activities and accomplishments of University of Minnesota faculty, colleges, departments, buildings, student organizations, and athletics. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1584]

title: Inventory of the Minnesota Geological and Natural History Survey Papers
long_description: The collection contains four letterpress volumes of correspondence by Ulysses Sherman Grant (1867-1932), a survey assistant, who administered the survey while Winchell traveled to Europe to study Minnesota clays and mineral deposits (vol. 1-4). There are also two volumes that record books and serials owned by Geological and Natural History Survey (vol. 5-6). The volumes were presumably part of a Winchell’s private collection that were given to the Department of Geology to form the Winchell Library of Geology in 1911. A bound ledger titled, “The Receipts and Disbursements of the Geological and Natural History Survey Funds” contains the “Report of the Geological Survey” written by Winchell, which outlines the original legislative act establishing the survey. It describes the sale of salt spring lands which, in addition to regular appropriations from the legislature, financed the execution of the survey. The ledger includes a chronological listing of all survey expenditures, including salary for field assistants, supply & equipment purchases, travel costs, etc., from August 1st, 1872-July 31st 1906. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1674]

title: Itasca Biological Station and Laboratories Records
long_description: The Itasca Biology Station records consist of correspondence, reports, committee minutes, grant materials, station histories, papers, publications and photographs related to biology instruction and field work conducted at the station. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1391]

title: John Gibler Papers
long_description: The John W. Gibler Papers include a wide range of wheat and crop breeding-related materials, including Gibler’s collection of journal articles, conference papers, plant-crossing ledgers and other technical and field-oriented materials. The materials cover the period when Gibler began his work in Mexico with Norman Borlaug in the early 1950s through the mid 1990s, when Gibler retired from consulting and international travel. The collection also includes work-related and personal correspondence. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1756]

title: John S. Pillsbury Papers
long_description: The John S. Pillsbury Papers document the relationship and work of John Sargent Pillsbury, former Minnesota Governor and University of Minnesota Regent, with the University of Minnesota, primarily through correspondence and also regarding land dealings. Documents and correspondence about mining and lumber, photographs, and biographical information on Pillsbury and his family are also included. The collection does not include information on Pillsbury Company or his other business ventures. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1487]

title: Junior F. Hayden Botanical Photograph Collection
long_description: Junior F. Hayden, a resident of Minneapolis, donated his botanical photography to the University of Minnesota's Department of Botany in 1950. Mr. Hayden's subject was the flora of Minnesota. The photographs consist of approximately 3,000 color Kodachrome slides of botanical specimens taken in the field and in the studio. Along with the slides, Mr. Hayden provided funds and instructions to make the Hayden Collection of Botanical Slides "larger, better, or more available for use." In 2000, Prof. Edward J. Cushing sent approximately 1,000 slides to the Kodak Company to be digitized. Bell Museum Curators, George Weiblen and Anita Cholewa, verified the names of plant species depicted in the digital images using the University of Minnesota herbarium database in 2011. The Hayden Botanical Slide Collection is part of the Department of Botany records available at the University of Minnesota Archives. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1673]

title: Katharine Jane Densford Papers
long_description: Collection contains the papers of Katharine Densford, professor and director of the School of Nursing at the University of Minnesota, including biographical information, correspondence, speeches, clippings, pictures, postcards, notebooks, information files on people, places, commissions, organizations and committees and published works in the field of nursing and health. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1669]

title: La Raza Student Cultural Organization Records
long_description: The collection contains records of the history and activities of La Raza Student Cultural Organization, which promotes greater historical, political and cultural awareness concerning the Chicano/a, Xicano/a and Latino/a communities, through cultural and educational programs and events. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1569]

title: Lloyd M. Short Papers
long_description: The Lloyd Short papers consists of personal and professional material from the beginning of his work in the Department of Political Science at the University of Minnesota in 1935 until his retirement in 1965. A bulk of the material includes associations, administrations and committees that Short was involved in, from 1924 to 1965, and includes material on his inclusion in the American Political Science Association and the Minneapolis Citizens’ League. Other documents include Short’s involvement in the Seoul National University (1955-1961) and the research produced during his directing of the Public Administration Center, now known as the Hubert H. Humphrey Institute of Public Affairs. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1045]

title: Margaret B. Davis Papers
long_description: The collection contains correspondence, research data and publications, teaching materials, and photo slides in sheets. Also, there are materials related to various conferences and meetings, including papers regarding the Desert Research Institute at the University of Nevada (1992-1993), Trends in Ecology and Evolution (1987-1995), and the American Quaternary Association (AMQUA). Most notably, a collection of field notebooks related to core samples collected by Davis were deposited in 2018 after long-term loan from the Limnological Research Center (LRC) at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1591]

title: Max Lowenthal Papers
long_description: Collection contains the papers of Max Lowenthal, alumnus of the University of Minnesota. A successful attorney who devoted his life to public service, Lowenthal served as counsel to a series of government committees in the 1930s and 1940s. Lowenthal may be best known for his work with the National Committee on Law Observance and Enforcement (the Wickersham Commission), the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, and the Interstate Commerce Commission. His second book, The Federal Bureau of Investigation(1950), was highly critical of the Bureau's covert political operations and director J. Edgar Hoover. Lowenthal was also a trusted friend and advisor to President Harry S. Truman and played a key role behind the Truman administration's recognition of Israel in 1948. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1715]

title: Minnesota Agricultural Experiment Station Records
long_description: The Minnesota Agricultural Experiment Station records contain materials concerning research, instruction, operations and events at the St Paul station occurring between 1882 and 2010. Most of the collection consists of correspondence, much of which is interfiled with minutes, reports, project proposals and agreements, planning documents, conference programs and proceedings, data on crops, land use and station expenditures, varietal certification, and documentation about departments involved in station activities, publications and government documents. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1657]

title: Minnesota Center for Philosophy of Science Records
long_description: Collection contains the records of the Minnesota Center for Philosophy of Science at the University of Minnesota. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1106]

title: Minnesota Geological Survey Field Notebooks
long_description: This collection consists of field notebooks created by the personnel of the Minnesota Geological Survey (MGS) and its predecessor, the Minnesota Geological and Natural History Survey (MGNHS). The notes include basic data used to compile annual reports and bulletins on geological matters. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1675]

title: Minnesota Geological Survey Papers
long_description: The collection contains correspondence, reports, conference and workshop materials, and other administrative papers of the Minnesota Geological Survey. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1676]

title: Minnesota’s Human Rights Stories Oral History Project
Moses Barron Papers
long_description: The collection contains materials relating to Barron's medical experiences in World War I and his work as a doctor and researcher at the University of Minnesota. Materials from the War include an extensive set of photographs of Base Hospital No. 26, of staff, and of activities of the men. Also included are clippings and memorabilia. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1705]

title: Myrtle Jeannette Eklund Papers
long_description: Collection contains correspondence of Myrtle Jeannette Eklund, librarian of the Public Affairs library at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1504]

title: N. L. (Neal) Gault, Jr. Papers
long_description: The collection contains correspondence, photographs, speeches, and subject files related to the American Legion and veterans health care, Seoul National University and other international medical education, and materials related to his role as Dean of the Medical School. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/6076]

title: Ned L. Huff Lantern Slide Collection
long_description: These slides depict plants, algae, fungus, and regional landscapes throughout Minnesota, the western United States, and Canada. The slides were created by Ned L. Huff (1876-1964), an instructor and assistant professor of botany from 1906-1945. Huff used the slides, many of which he hand-colored, to illustrate general botany lectures and the course titled, “Minnesota Plant Life,” offered by the University Extension Division. Huff attended the Minnesota Seaside Station in 1903, 1906, and 1907. Several slides depict station life as well as interactions with the Pacheedaht First Nation. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1673]

title: Newton Horace Winchell Papers
long_description: The collection contains field notebooks Winchell kept while he conducted geological observations of Minnesota as State Geologist of the Minnesota Geological and Natural History Survey (MGNHS). The notebooks, which contain records of stones, outcroppings, deposits, etc., were used to compile the twenty-four annual reports Winchell authored and submitted to the Board of Regents between 1872 and 1899. Two notebooks in Box 1, Folder 3, record Winchell’s 1874 trip to the Black Hills in the Dakota Territory, where he served as a field geologist for a military and scientific expedition lead by General George A. Custer. Winchell obtained several specimens for the General Museum during the trip as well. Two notebooks in Box 2, Folder 2, document Winchell’s travel and study in Paris from May 1, 1895 – May 1896, where he studied Minnesota rocks in the laboratory of Professor Lacroix, noted mineralogist and petrographer. The collection also contains scrapbooks (Box 2, Volumes 1-2) of newspaper clippings that document articles published about the MGNHS, as well as broader geological issues. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1694]

title: Norman E. Borlaug Papers
long_description: The collection consists of the personal and professional papers of Norman E. Borlaug, including, correspondence, publications, field notes, speeches and lectures, photographs, and awards and honorary degrees. Borlaug is primarily known as the public face of “The Green Revolution,” an international scientific and political alignment during the 1950s and 1960s that produced a worldwide shift in crop production methods. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1743]

title: Norman W. Moen Papers
long_description: Collection contains the papers of Norman W. Moen, professor emeritus in General College at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1361]

title: Office of the President Records
long_description: The President of the University of Minnesota serves as the chief executive officer of the University and ex officio president of the Board of Regents. With offices on the Twin Cities campus, the president is supported by an executive team that includes senior vice presidents, vice presidents, general counsel, University coordinate campus chancellors, director of athletics, and president of the University of Minnesota Foundation. These records document the administrative role and activities of the Office of the President at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1644]

title: Office of the Senior VP for System Academic Administration Records
long_description: Contains records of the Office of the Senior Vice President for System Academic Administration, the office responsible for system-wide academic administration and outreach throughout University system between 2004-2012 and selected biographical information, awards, correspondence and speeches for Dr. Robert Jones, who headed the office from 2006 to 2012. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1557]

title: Office of the Vice President for Academic Administration Papers
long_description: Collection contains the papers of the Office of the Vice President for Academic Administration at the University of Minnesota. They cover the vice presidency of Malcolm M. Willey (1943-1963) as well as his tenure as University dean and assistant to the president (1934-1943). [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1645]

title: Office of the Vice President for Academic Administration Records
long_description: Records consist of the files of the Vice President for Academic Administration at the University of Minnesota during the tenure of William G. Shepherd. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1313]

title: Office of the Vice President for Student Affairs Records
long_description: This collection both precedes and follows the period that Paul Cashman was Vice President (1968-1975) and includes the transition period between Edmund G. Williamson as the dean of students and Cashman as vice president of student affairs. The records reflect a period of student protests and change at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1314]

title: Philosophical Psychology Lectures
long_description: Lectures on the topic of Philosophical Psychology recorded at the University of Minnesota during the spring semester of 1989.

title: Richard Maurice Elliott Papers
long_description: The collection consists of the papers of Richard M. Elliott, professor and chairman of the Psychology Department at the University of Minnesota (1919-1956). The papers contain Elliott's personal and professional correspondence, lecture notes, history of the Psychology Department and work with the Appleton Century Crofts publishing company. The papers also contain information on Mathilde Rice Elliott. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1670]

title: Senior and Agrarian School of Agriculture Yearbooks
long_description: The School of Agriculture records consist of correspondence, scrapbooks, student lists, service records of school faculty members, statistics, committee materials, meeting minutes, club record books, materials relating to school activities including livestock judging, cultural programming and sporting events, records of student projects and yearbooks from the School of Agriculture at the University of Minnesota’s St. Paul campus, also known as University Farm. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1264]

title: Stephen Farnham Peckham Papers
long_description: This collection contains the following items: the autograph of John Johnson Enmegahbowh, an Indian Episcopal clergyman. A holograph manuscript report dated 1877 describing the examination of the Red River valley water supply by Dr. C. N. Hewitt, Professor N. H. Winchell and himself. A holograph manuscript describing the meteor which fell in Iowa, May 10, 1878. A holograph manuscript dated 1878 which in semi-diary form describes his activities of that year. A holograph manuscript describing a trip on the Upper Missouri River dated 1880 (He also discusses in considerable detail an Indian dance he saw). A report of the evidence given before the coroner's jury on the explosion at the Washburn "A" Mill in 1878, together with supporting reports and documents. Copies of eight of Professor Peckham's publications on various subjects. A holograph reminiscence dated 1877 entitled "School suffrage for women in Minnesota and how it worked". [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1482]

title: Student Activities Bureau Papers
long_description: The Student Activities Bureau Papers contains the records of student activities at the University of Minnesota beginning in 1911, with the bulk of the materials comprised of the papers of the Student Activities Bureau (SAB) from its inception in 1943 until 1970. The collection contains membership lists, correspondence, reports, publications by the staff of SAB and articles regarding student activities, surveys, meeting minutes, materials regarding campus orientation, financial papers, data sheets, faculty polls, staff assignments, roster cards, employee applications, materials regarding off-campus agencies, SAB office procedures, and on-campus projects and programs papers. The papers of various student organizations, including academic, religious, social, cultural, political, and recreational, are contained in the collection. Also, a large portion of the collection consists of materials regarding many of the fraternities and sororities established at the University of Minnesota over the years. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1708]

title: Tracy F. Tyler Papers
long_description: The collection documents Tracy Tyler's national role in broadcast and radio education. Materials include correspondence, speeches, and writings with such groups as the American Council on Education's Advisory Committee on Education, National Committee on Education by Radio, and the Federal Radio Education Committee. The collection contains very little material regarding Dr. Tyler's role at the University of Minnesota. There are a few folders of correspondence between Tyler and various University presidents. One item of note is an original copy of the 1959 agreement between the University of Minnesota and the International Cooperation Administration regarding the rebuilding of Seoul National University. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1238]

title: University of Minnesota Archives Audio Collection
long_description: Historical audio recordings held by the University of Minnesota Archives.

title: University of Minnesota Archives Photograph Collection
long_description: Photographs of University of Minnesota campuses, people, and activities, 1870s - present. Includes images of staff, faculty, students, buildings, construction, classes, research, athletics, artworks.

title: University of Minnesota Archives Scrapbook Collection
long_description: Collection contains scrapbooks assembled by alumni, students, and organizations highlighting various histories of the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1613]

title: University of Minnesota Archives Video Collection
long_description: Footage of University of Minnesota events and activities. Includes athletics, lectures, commencement ceremonies, concerts, and experiments.

title: University of Minnesota Athletics Records
long_description: Collection contains reports, correspondence, media guides, budgetary information, policies, committee meetings, and clippings that document student athletics at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1666]

title: University of Minnesota Gopher Yearbooks
long_description: 82 volumes of the Gopher yearbook, published between 1888-1967. An additional volume was published for the 1982-1983 academic year. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/5820]

title: University Relations Records
long_description: Collection contains the records of University Relations at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1681]

title: Verna Golden Scott Papers
long_description: The collection consists of correspondence with booking agents and publicity material regarding artists engaged by Scott to perform at the University of Minnesota and other venues. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1293]

title: William Skinner Cooper Papers
long_description: The collection consists of personal and professional papers of William Skinner Cooper, professor of botany at the University of Minnesota. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/5824]

title: William W. Folwell Papers
long_description: This collection contains personal papers of William Watts Folwell, first president of the University of Minnesota (1869-1883). It includes materials from his student days; scholarly, instructional, and civic writings; and documents and correspondence from his time as an university administrator. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources/1686]

title: Alan Rich Papers
long_description: This collection contains mostly letters about daily life to Alan Rich while he served in the army during World War II, as well as some of his replys to his wife, Poppy. Also included are drafts of a short autobiography, holiday cards, newsletters from Alan Rich's army base, photographs of the Rich family and of his time in the war, newspaper clippings, marriage certificate, immigration papers, document of name change, and the 1926 Menorah Annual. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/501]

title: Amos S. Deinard Papers
long_description: his collection consists of personal and professional papers collected by Amos S. Deinard. The first series, covering personal papers, includes newspaper clippings, correspondence, and pamphlets related to members of the Deinard family and dates from 1895 to 1986. The second series, covering organizational papers, includes reports, correspondence, fliers, and programs for events for organizations that Deinard was involved or interested in throughout the community; most of these materials are from local and national organizations and date from 1911 to 1983. The third series is pamphlets and small publications, mostly from national and international organizations, related to topics that interested Deinard, namely antisemitism and Zionism, and the materials date from 1895 to 1976. In this series each publication is listed by title and author, if this information was included on the publication. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/484]

title: Berman Family Papers
long_description: The correspondence between Rose (Berman) Goldstein and her family is mostly about daily life; there is little mention about World War II. Most correspondence dates between 1918 - 1947, and is written from Minneapolis, Minnesota and Sacramento, California to the Twin Cities and New York. Other locations include Chicago, IL; Omaha, NE; Lake Geneva, WI; Jerusalem, Israel; Italy; and Russia. There are letters speaking to graduations, marriages, birth, travels, and death, as well as fur and leather-goods trade in California, medical situations, and religious life. Items include postcards, telegrams, wedding invitations, periodicals, newsletters, newspaper clippings, programs, published material, family writings, correspondence, and letters. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/531]

title: Burton Rudolph Papers
long_description: This collection contains papers of the Rudolph and Kaner families relating to their family history, businesses, and correspondence in Yiddish with relatives in Lithuania, some of which are translated. The photographs, black and white and in color, are mostly of family members. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/525]

title: Frank and Arthur Eisenberg Papers
long_description: This collection documents the experiences of a Minneapolis Jewish family in which father and son served in World War I and World War II, respectively. Contains correspondences with family and friends, military records, travel materials, personal writings, photographs, news and entertainment articles, childhood and professional ephemera, and religious items. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/463]

title: Harold and Zelda Goldenberg Family Papers
long_description: This collection consists primarily of Harold Goldenberg's letters to Zelda Goldberg while he was attending Harvard Law School, 1928-1931. Harold was president of the Minneapolis Federation for Jewish Service from 1943-1946, and chairman of the United Jewish Appeal, 1945-1950. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/7273]

title: Hillel of the University of Minnesota Records
long_description: This collection consists of administrative records related to the Hillel organization at the University of Minnesota and date between 1929 and 2016. The collection includes correspondence; meeting minutes; programming and event planning including event ephemera such as posters, ticket stubs, fliers and buttons; clippings; and planning documents such as constitutions and by-laws. This collection also includes 1.61MB of electronic records, which consist of 74 digitally-born Word documents of board meeting minutes. Please note that access to these materials is limited to an on-site computer in our reading room. [Finding Aid at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/541]

title: Jack Pink Papers
long_description: This collection consists of one journal, some ephemeral materials including posters and a troop station billet tag, correspondence, and one newspaper clipping. Materials are dated between 1918 and 1958. The journal is handwritten in a leather bound notebook; the pages are delicate and so the journal has been digitized. The journal includes detail of time spent at Camp Dodge before being sent to various locations around France throughout 1918. [Finding aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/545]

title: Jeanette and Kenneth Frank Papers
long_description: This collection consists of a scrapbook that includes photographs and Yiddish newspaper clippings related to a Yiddish theater troupe in a German displaced persons camp after the end of World War II. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/9627]

title: Jewish Community Relations Council Records
long_description: This collection consists of the administrative records of the Jewish Community Relations Council, a non-profit organization that acts as the public affairs voice of the Jewish community in Minnesota and the Dakotas. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/488]

title: Jewish Fellowship Club Records
long_description: This collection consists of administrative materials dating between 1927 and 1999 and includes: meeting minutes; financial materials; correspondence; event planning documents; newsletters; ephemera such as stationary, ticket stubs, coat check room tickets; newspaper clippings in scrapbook pages; and planning documents for a Twin Ports Jewish reunion which took place in 1985. The collection also includes two scrapbooks relating to the Jewish Social Service Agency, as well as various materials related to Temple Emanuel. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/7172]

title: Jewish Fellowship News
long_description: Jewish Fellowship News was a Duluth, Minnesota based newspaper published by the Jewish Fellowship Club, whose origins date back to 1935. The Jewish Fellowship News was a monthly newspaper that became the designated publication of the organized Jewish communities of the twin ports of Duluth, Minnesota and Superior, Wisconsin, and was published through the early 2000s.

title: Jewish Historical Society of the Upper Midwest Media Collection
long_description: This collection consists of various types of media collected from various donors, given to the Jewish Historical Society of the Upper Midwest between the years 1984 and 2013. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/542]

title: Jewish Historical Society of the Upper Midwest Oral History Collection
long_description: This collection consists of various cassette tapes of recorded oral histories from various projects that were donated and organized by the Jewish Historical Society of the Upper Midwest. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/485]

title: Jewish History Collection
long_description: This collection consists of various small donations of materials from various people related to the Jewish communities of Minnesota, North and South Dakota.

title: Lincoln Del Collection
long_description: This collection consists of memorabilia from The Lincoln Del, a Jewish Deli with branches in Minneapolis and the western suburbs. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/7719]

title: Minnesota Synagogues Collection
long_description: This collection consists of various materials from synagogues throughout Minnesota including: Adath Jeshurun, Beth El, Sons of Abraham, Temple of Aaron, and Temple Israel. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/7455]

title: Mount Sinai Hospital Auxiliary Records
long_description: Records include administrative materials such as correspondence, meeting minutes and financial statements of funds raised. Some administrative materials related to Mt. Sinai Hospital directly and not to the Auxiliary are also included. Newsletters include those directly from the Auxiliary as well as Mt. Sinai Hospital employee newsletters. Scrapbooks of news clippings and public relations surrounding the hospital are included. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/457]

title: Mount Zion Temple Oral History Records
long_description: All of the materials in this collection are electronic records, including mp3 files for the oral histories themselves as well as corresponding word documents, pdfs, and jps of miscellaneous documents and transcripts related to the oral histories. All oral histories were conducted between 2003 and 2013. The oral histories are broken into thematic groups: one documents Holocaust survivors, a second documents stories related to social justice within the Jewish community, and a third is general oral histories. The Holocaust Survivors and Social Justice oral histories were conducted specifically for the 150th anniversary project, while the others were conducted separately from that project. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/543]

title: Project to Document Early Jewish Settlers in Minnesota Records
long_description: This collection contains materials for research and includes handwritten notes on paper and index cards, newspaper clippings, correspondence, brochures, photocopies for research, three floppy discs and four magnetic reel to reel tapes. All material dated between 1864 and 2002, with the bulk of materials dating in the 1980s. The collection is broken into two series: Series 1 deals with administrative materials related to the project, as well as subject files related to organizations, synagogues, and cities; Series 2 deals with specific families for which Marilyn found information, either through oral history interviews or through her research of primary documents. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/538]

title: Rabbi Harold H. Gordon Papers
long_description: This collection consists of photographs from scrapbooks that Rabbi Harold H. Gordon created while working as an Army Air Force chaplain beginning in 1942, documenting his travels around the United States, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Egypt, and more. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/519]

title: Resort Discrimination Records
long_description: This collection consists of letters and pamphlets relating to the discrimination of guests; specifically of the Jewish religion, to resorts, hotels, and lodges in northern Minnesota, Ontario, Canada, and north western Wisconsin. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/503]

title: Richard Harris Papers
long_description: This collection consists of materials from the B.W. Harris Manufacturing Company and Zero King Outerware. This includes: photos, correspondence, news clippings, history, fashion books, catalogs, a button, and fabric samples. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/7654]

title: Sharron and Oren Steinfeldt Collection
long_description: This collection is comprised entirely of photographs dating between 1860 and 2010 and oral history interviews. The photographs are in black-and-white and color, of varying dimensions. The oral histories originate from several projects undertaken by the Upper Midwest Jewish Archives through the years. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/492]

title: Sidney Cohen Papers
long_description: This collection consists of four log books detailing Sidney Cohen's time spent in the Hospital Corp of the United States Navy during World War I. [Finding Aid available at: http://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/502]

title: Soviet Jewry Action Newsletter
long_description: This Soviet Jewry Action Newsletter was published by the Jewish Community Relations Council, a non-profit organization that acts as the public affairs voice of the Jewish community in Minnesota and the Dakotas. These digitized newsletters are part of the Jewish Community Relations Council collection (UMJA0013) at the University of Minnesota's Upper Midwest Jewish Archives. Additional materials from the Jewish Community Relations Council collection have also been digitized and are available on this site. [Finding aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/488]

title: Soviet Women - Old Lives, New Lives Oral History Project
long_description: Why do people decide to leave the land of their birth and start over? What was life like for Jews in the Soviet Union and specifically for Jewish women? What did mothers want for their children? How did it feel to be labeled “Jew” in the Soviet Union and “Russian” in America? What do American Jews expect of newcomers and how realistic are these expectations? These were among the questions put to a group of women who entered the St. Paul Jewish community beginning in 1978. In the course of lengthy oral history interviews, the women--ranging in age and background--talked candidly about their lives, past and present.

title: Talmud Torah of Minneapolis Records
long_description: This collection consists of documents relating to administration, students and alumni, and various events and clubs within the Talmud Torah of Minneapolis from the early to late twentieth century. Materials are in both English and Hebrew. The materials are not comprehensive and there are numerous gaps. [Finding Aid available at: https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/15/resources/529]

title: Talmud Torah of St. Paul Records
